Strain the tea into the mug (straining is optional, the spices settle to the bottom).
Rinse the saucepan, add 60 ml (1/4 cup) milk and 0.5 tbsp maple syrup, and heat to 150F (65C): hot with small bubbles at the edges but not simmering.
Froth the milk with a hand frother, whisk or French press, then let the foam rest about 30 seconds.
Pour the milk and foam into the mug, sprinkle with extra chai spices and serve.
verified_note: Halved to 1 small serving. Water + black tea bag brewed -> black_tea:120. Homemade chai spice blend (0.5 tsp) has no id and is not listed on the page's ingredient line; left unmapped. Maple syrup 1 tbsp halved to 0.5 tbsp. Not included: homemade chai spice blend (0.5 tsp)

name: Mexican Coffee
steps: Heat 1 cup (240 ml) water, 1 whole clove, 1/4 cinnamon stick and 2 tbsp brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add 1 tbsp regular-grind coffee and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir, cover and remove from heat.
Let the grounds settle, then pour into a mug (or strain into the mug).
verified_note: Page does not state servings; assumed 4 mugs from 4 cups water, so everything divided by 4 (2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 clove, 1/4 cinnamon stick, 1 tbsp coffee). Brown sugar -> simple_syrup:2tbsp. Ground coffee has no id (only brewed espresso/instant). Food Network version was rejected because it contains coffee liqueur. Not included: regular grind coffee (1 tbsp)

name: Café de Olla
steps: Heat water with piloncillo (or jaggery), ground coffee and a cinnamon stick, stirring until the sugar dissolves
Bring to a boil, take off the heat and steep 5 minutes
Strain into mugs and serve hot

name: Café Bombón
steps: Carefully pour 2 oz (60 ml) sweetened condensed milk into a small glass.
Hold a teaspoon over the milk and slowly pour 1 oz (30 ml) espresso over the back (convex side) of the spoon so it runs gently on top.
Serve showing the two layers, and stir before drinking.
verified_note: Recipe card uses 2:1 condensed milk to espresso (the article text mentions 1:1 as the usual ratio).

name: Café con Leche
steps: Make 4 oz (1/2 cup) strong coffee in a Moka pot, or pull an espresso shot.
Steam 4 oz (1/2 cup) whole milk with an espresso machine, stretching it to 20 to 25 percent in height. Or froth it with a frother, French press or whisk.
Pour the coffee into a cup and stir in 1 to 2 teaspoons sugar.
Add the steamed milk and serve immediately.
verified_note: Sugar (1 to 2 tsp, 1.5 used) mapped to simple_syrup. Page offers oat milk as a dairy-free option. Espresso 120 ml means 4 oz strong coffee (Moka pot or espresso).

name: Flat White
steps: Brew 36 g espresso.
Pour 120 ml cold milk into a clean pitcher, up to just below the spout.
Steam the milk adding only a small amount of air (usually a couple of seconds). It should be thin and glossy with no visible bubbles; steam to 60-65C (do not go above 70C).
Knock the pitcher gently on the counter and swirl the milk to remove large bubbles.
Starting low, pour the milk into the espresso at an angle, swirling gently to combine.
When the cup is about two-thirds full, bring the pitcher closer to the surface and keep pouring while straightening the cup.
verified_note: Espresso given as 36 g liquid, entered as 36 ml.

name: Apple Crisp Macchiato
steps: Make the apple syrup: combine 1 large diced Granny Smith apple, 1 cup apple cider, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup light brown sugar and 2 cinnamon sticks in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low and cook 10 minutes until the apples are tender and the sugar has dissolved.
Remove from the heat and let steep 15 minutes.
Strain through a fine mesh sieve, pressing on the apples to extract flavor. Refrigerate in an airtight container (makes enough for many drinks).
Pour 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and 2 to 3 teaspoons of the apple syrup into a tall glass.
Fill the glass with ice and top with 1 shot freshly brewed espresso. Drizzle with extra syrup if you like.
For a hot drink, heat the milk and skip the ice.
verified_note: Homemade apple-cinnamon syrup mapped to simple_syrup (12 ml = 2 to 3 tsp). Page's main version is iced; hot version given as a tip. Our hot mug version is covered by the tip. Not included: Apple-cinnamon syrup (homemade)

name: Gingerbread Latte
steps: Make the gingerbread syrup (brown sugar syrup simmered 20 minutes with fresh ginger, allspice berries and cinnamon sticks; the page gives no amounts here).
Brew 2 shots (2 oz / 60 ml) espresso with an espresso machine, manual espresso maker, French press or moka pot.
Stir 1 tbsp gingerbread syrup into the espresso.
Steam or froth 4 oz (1/2 cup, 120 ml) whole or oat milk.
Pour the milk into the center of the espresso so a light foam sits on top.
Sprinkle with cinnamon if you like.
verified_note: Gingerbread syrup (linked recipe, amounts not on page) -> closest id brown_sugar_syrup, 1 tbsp. Syrup contains ginger, allspice, cinnamon. Not included: gingerbread syrup (exact recipe not on page)

name: Peppermint Mocha
steps: Heat 3/4 cup (180 ml) milk with 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder and 1/8 tsp peppermint extract in a saucepan until boiling, then remove from heat.
Froth the mixture with a milk frother or immersion blender.
Pour the peppermint chocolate mixture over 2 oz (60 ml) espresso (or 1 cup brewed coffee).
Top with whipped cream, crushed candy canes and/or chocolate shavings if you like.
garnish: whipped cream, crushed candy canes, chocolate shavings
verified_note: Sugar 3 tbsp -> simple_syrup:3tbsp. Peppermint extract 1/8 tsp has no id (mint is fresh leaves) so left unmapped. Not included: peppermint extract (1/8 tsp)

name: Pistachio Latte (Hot)
steps: Put 1 cup (240 ml) milk, 2 tbsp (30 g) pistachio butter (or pistachio cream) and 1 tbsp maple syrup (or other sweetener, if you want it sweet) in a saucepan. Stir, then heat over medium just until hot, about 150°F (65°C) on a cooking thermometer.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1/4 tsp pure vanilla extract.
Whisk or froth the milk mixture until small bubbles form.
Pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot espresso or strong brewed coffee into a mug. Once the milk foam settles, slowly pour the milk over the coffee, garnish and serve.
verified_note: Pistachio butter/cream mapped to nuts (30g). Vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup (closest). Page does not name a garnish; the page also has an iced variation (not used).

name: Billionaire's Latte
steps: Spoon 2 tablespoons caramel into your serving mug or glass to form a bottom layer.
Add 3 to 4 pieces of chocolate (dark, milk or white), either melted or whole; they will melt when the hot coffee is poured over them.
Prepare 1 shot of espresso and pour it into the glass.
Heat 120 ml whole milk, then froth it with a milk frother.
Pour the milk into the glass so the foam sits on top.
Sprinkle 1 crushed shortbread cookie over the top and serve immediately.
verified_note: 3-4 chocolate pieces approximated as chocolate_syrup:15 (about 15 g chocolate). Espresso shot taken as 30 ml. Shortbread has no id. Not included: Shortbread cookie, 1, crumbled

name: Eggnog Latte
steps: Pour 2 oz (60 ml) espresso into a mug.
Combine 1/2 cup (120 ml) eggnog and 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk in a milk steamer and steam them according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Pour the steamed eggnog-milk mixture into the mug and spoon the foam on top.
Optionally sprinkle with freshly grated nutmeg.
verified_note: Store-bought eggnog (1/2 cup / 120 ml) has no id and is left unmapped; closest approximation would be milk plus cream plus egg yolk but the page does not use those. Not included: eggnog (120 ml)

name: Ruby Chocolate Latte
steps: Heat water in a kettle (the page sets the kettle to 60°C). Put 1/2 tsp ground coffee (page: 1 tsp for 2 cups) in a cafetiere and pour in about 30 ml of the hot water (the author says 60 ml for the 2-cup batch; the amount is not on the recipe card).
Let the coffee brew for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir with a wooden spoon and scoop off the grounds floating on top, then press the plunger all the way down.
Bring 175 ml whole milk to a gentle boil in a pan.
Add 35 g ruby chocolate to the milk and stir well until melted.
Pour the coffee into the chocolate milk and mix well. Serve hot in a glass.
verified_note: Ruby chocolate has no id; mapped to white_chocolate (closest, ruby is a pink cocoa-butter based chocolate). Brewed cafetiere coffee mapped to espresso:30. Water for brewing is not on the card; 60 ml for 2 cups comes from an author comment. Halved from 2 servings. Page also says it can be cooled and served over ice.

name: Coconut Milk Coffee (Hot)
steps: Pull a single shot of espresso, or brew strong coffee with a French press, moka pot or other maker.
Heat 1 cup (250 ml) unsweetened coconut milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until warm but not boiling, about 2 to 3 minutes (or microwave in 15-second intervals until warm and steaming).
Froth the milk until foamy and velvety with a steam wand, hand frother or a jar with a lid.
Pour the hot coffee into your cup and stir in 1 to 2 tsp sweetener.
Slowly pour the frothed milk over the coffee, holding back the foam with the back of a spoon, then spoon the foam on top.
Stir and drink.
verified_note: Page gives 'single shot' with no ml; 30 ml assumed as one standard shot. Sweetener 1-2 tsp -> maple_syrup 1.5tsp. Optional 1/2 tsp vanilla/coconut extract and nutmeg/cinnamon garnish skipped.

name: South Indian Filter Coffee
steps: Brew a strong decoction with ground filter coffee
Put sugar in the tumbler, add hot milk, then the decoction
Pour back and forth between tumbler and dabara 2 to 3 times to froth

name: Thai Spiced Iced Tea
steps: Bring 1 1/4 cups (about 295 ml) water to a boil in a small saucepan.

Remove from the heat and add about 1 1/8 tsp loose black or red Thai tea (or 1 1/2 tea bags), 1/2 star anise and 3/4 of a clove (about 1 clove and a piece of star anise is fine), keeping everything submerged. Steep for 10 minutes.
Strain out the tea, star anise and clove.
Stir in 1/2 tbsp sugar until fully dissolved, then let the tea cool to room temperature.
Fill a tall glass with ice and pour in the tea until it is about 3/4 full.
Add 1 tbsp sweetened condensed milk, stir and drink right away.
verified_note: Divided by 4. black_tea:295 is the brewed tea volume (water 5 cups / 4). Star anise (0.5) and cloves (0.75) both map to the clove id, so clove:0.75pcs covers the cloves and the star anise is mentioned in the steps. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page uses sweetened condensed milk, not evaporated milk.

name: Earl Grey Fog & Tonic
steps: Pour 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water over 1 tbsp loose-leaf Earl Grey tea and let it steep for 30 minutes.
Let the tea cool, then stir in 1 tsp fresh lemon juice.
Strain the tea into a tall glass filled with ice, filling it about half to three-quarters full.
Top with about 1/2 cup (120 ml) tonic water and stir. Use more tea than tonic or half and half, to taste.
verified_note: Page uses diet tonic; mapped to tonic. Page makes 2 servings (2 tbsp tea, 2 cups boiling water, 1 cup tonic, 2 tsp lemon juice), halved. Tea brewed amount counted as earl_grey:240.

name: Peach Rosemary Iced Tea
steps: Bring 1/2 cup (about 107 ml) water to a boil, remove from the heat, add about 1/4 of a tea bag (the page uses 2 bags per 9 cups) and 2/3 of a rosemary sprig, and steep 5 minutes. Remove the tea bag.
Stir in 1 tbsp sugar until dissolved and let the rosemary steep 15 more minutes. Remove the rosemary.
Pour the tea into a large glass or jar, add another 1/2 cup (about 107 ml) water and about 50 g (2 oz) sliced peaches (fresh or frozen), and cover.
Let it sit at room temperature for about 1 hour, then refrigerate so the peaches steep overnight (up to 5 days).
Serve over ice, garnished with a rosemary sprig.
verified_note: Divided by 9 (page: 8 cups water, 2 tea bags, 6 rosemary sprigs, 1 cup sugar, 1 lb peaches, makes about 9 cups). Brewed tea mapped to black_tea in ml (4 cups/9 = 107 ml); extra water 107 ml. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp. Page gives no glass.

name: Matcha Vanilla Swirl
steps: Fill your serving glass with ice.
Blend 3 tbsp rolled oats, 1 tsp maple syrup, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, a pinch of sea salt and 3/4 cup (180 ml) filtered water on high for about 1 minute until smooth.
Pour this oat milk through a fine mesh strainer into the glass of ice, pressing the pulp with a spoon so all the liquid passes through.

Sift 1 tsp matcha into a small wide bowl. Add a little of 1/3 cup (80 ml) hot water that has been off the boil for about a minute and whisk hard until dissolved. Add the rest of the hot water and whisk again until frothy.
Pour the matcha over the iced oat milk and stir to combine.
verified_note: No page titled Matcha Vanilla Swirl was found; used this vanilla oat iced matcha latte as the closest real recipe. Homemade oat milk (oats plus water) mapped to oat_milk:180. Vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup (0.5 tsp); maple syrup 1 tsp. Oats and salt not listed as ids. Not included: rolled oats 3 tbsp (inside homemade oat milk), sea salt pinch

name: Matcha Island
steps: Add 2 oz (60 ml) Ritual Gin Alternative, 1 oz (30 ml) cream of coconut, 1/2 oz (15 ml) lemon juice and 1/2 tsp matcha powder to a shaker with ice and shake thoroughly.
Double-strain into a glass, then add ice.
verified_note: Cream of coconut (sweetened) mapped to coconut_milk. Glass type not given by page. This is a Ritual Gin Alternative recipe from a brand blog, no pineapple. Not included: Ritual Gin Alternative 60 ml (branded non-alcoholic gin)

name: Masala Chai
steps: Bring water to a gentle boil with the crushed whole spices and ginger
Add the tea leaves and simmer 1 to 2 minutes
Add milk and sugar, bring to a boil and simmer a minute, then strain into cups

name: Adrak Chai (Ginger Tea)
steps: Heat 150 ml water in a pot. Add about 4 g (roughly 1.5 tsp) peeled, grated fresh ginger and 1.5 tsp loose leaf black tea. Bring to a rolling boil, then simmer on medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until the chai turns dark. (Boil the ginger in water before adding milk or the milk can curdle.)
Add 90 ml whole milk and bring to a boil on medium-high heat. Reduce the heat and bring it to a boil again.
Reduce the heat completely. Stir in 1.5 tsp sugar, 1/8 tsp ground cardamom and 1/8 tsp ground black pepper (optional but recommended: a pinch, about 1/8 tsp, of dried ground ginger).
Mix well and aerate the tea with a ladle 4 to 5 times. Turn off the heat, cover the pot and let it rest 3 to 4 minutes.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Page makes 2: halved. Page range for ginger is 3/4-1 tbsp (7-10 g) per 2 servings, so about 4 g each. Optional dried ground ginger has no separate id and is only in the steps. Loose tea given as 1 tbsp for 2, so 1.5 tsp each; black_tea id is brewed tea but used as dry leaf amount, as in our other chai.

name: Elaichi Chai (Cardamom Tea)
steps: Crush 1 tbsp whole cardamom with a pestle and mortar.
Add the crushed cardamom, 2 tsp loose black tea and 1/4 cup (60 ml) water to a milk pan.
Bring the water to a boil and let it reduce slightly.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk and 1 to 2 tsp sugar.
Boil the milk and let the tea cook for about 5 minutes.
Strain through a fine strainer into a cup and enjoy hot.
verified_note: Sugar 1-2 tsp mapped to simple_syrup:1.5tsp. Black tea is loose leaf (tsp), not brewed. Cardamom amount is 1 tbsp whole as written.

name: Doodh Patti Chai
steps: Put 360 ml (1.5 cups) whole milk in a pot with 2 lightly crushed cardamom pods and a very small piece of cinnamon (about 1 cm). Bring to a boil. (Tip: lay a heatproof spoon across the pot to stop it boiling over.)
Once the milk has boiled, aerate it with a ladle a few times.
Add about 1 tsp loose tea leaves (or 1 tea bag) and bring to a boil again.
Aerate a few times with a ladle and keep at an aggressive simmer for at least 5 minutes, until reduced by at least a third.
Strain and serve in a mug. (Sugar is listed on the page as 'to taste' with no amount or step.)
verified_note: Page's 1 serving is 2 cups (480 ml) milk with 1/2 tbsp tea and 3 pods; scaled to 3/4 (360 ml milk, about 3/8 tbsp tea, about 2 cardamom pods) to stay under 450 ml. Sugar is 'to taste' with no amount, so omitted from ings.

name: Karak Chai
steps: Boil 1 cup (240 ml) water in a saucepan.
Crush 2 to 3 cardamom pods (2.5 pods), about 1/4 inch of cinnamon bark and 1/2 tbsp grated ginger.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon, ginger and 1.5 tsp loose black tea to the water.
Bring to a boil, then add 1/2 cup (120 ml) evaporated milk (or whole milk).
Add 1 tsp sugar.
Bring to a rolling boil and boil for at least 3 to 4 minutes, until the tea is a dark caramel color and has thickened, then turn off the heat.
Strain through a tea strainer into a cup and serve.
verified_note: Page makes 2 cups (1 cup milk, 2 cups water, 3 tsp tea, 2 tsp sugar, 5 cardamom pods, 1/2 inch cinnamon bark, 1 tbsp ginger), halved. Cinnamon bark 1/4 inch approximated as 0.25tsp. No saffron in source.

name: Kesar Chai (Saffron Tea)
steps: Add 1 cup (240 ml) water and 5 saffron strands to a saucepan and bring to a brisk boil.
Once boiling, add 1/2 tsp tea leaves and simmer for about a minute, then turn off the heat.
Let the tea brew briefly so it stays light and does not turn bitter.
Stir in 2 tbsp (30 ml) milk and let it rest for a few seconds.
Strain into a cup, add a few more saffron strands on top and serve hot.
verified_note: Divided by 2. Page says 1 tsp tea leaves for 2; black_tea here is dry leaf (tsp), not brewed tea. Saffron 10 strands for 2 = 5 per cup, about 1 pinch.

name: Lemon Ginger Tea
steps: Remove 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water from the heat and add a 1/2 inch piece of ginger, thinly sliced, and 1/4 of a lemon, sliced.
Steep for about 20 minutes, then strain.
Serve warm (or pour over crushed ice for iced). Stir in honey if you like.
verified_note: Divided by 4. Ginger 2 inch piece = 0.5 inch, mapped as ginger:0.5pcs. Lemon is sliced into the tea, not juiced. Honey is optional with no amount given, so it is left out of ings. Page does not name a glass; mug is our assumption of a cup for warm tea.

name: Iced Chai Latte
steps: Make the concentrate: put 1 cup water, about 1 tsp chai spice blend (1.5 tbsp for 4 servings), 1 black tea bag and 1 tbsp maple syrup in a small saucepan and bring just to a boil.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes, then remove the tea bag and strain.
To serve, fill a glass with ice, then combine 3/4 cup (180 ml) concentrate with 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk.
verified_note: Page makes 4 servings of homemade concentrate (4 cups water, 1.5 tbsp chai spices, 4 tea bags, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 cup milk); homemade concentrate mapped to chai_concentrate. Per-serving concentrate ingredient amounts divided by 4.

name: Chai Blossom Soda
steps: Put 1/2 chai tea bag in 60 ml (1/4 cup) boiling water in a small bowl, cover and steep 8 to 10 minutes. (The page makes 4 drinks from 2 tea bags and 1 cup boiling water, so scale up as needed.)
Add 2 tbsp sugar and stir until dissolved. Remove the tea bag and let the mixture cool.
Mix the cooled chai syrup with 30 ml (2 tbsp) fresh lime juice.
Fill a rocks glass with ice, add the chai-lime mixture, and top with 75 ml (2 to 3 oz) club soda.
Garnish with a star anise pod and a lemon twist.
verified_note: Page makes 4: divided by 4. Home-steeped chai tea syrup mapped to chai_concentrate; sugar to simple_syrup. Club soda 2-3 oz per glass (page: 8-12 oz for 4).

name: Classic Southern Sweet Tea
steps: Steep strong black tea and stir the sugar in while it is hot
Dilute with cool water and chill
Serve over ice

name: Chamomile Honey Iced Tea
steps: Bring water to a boil and let it rest about 60 seconds (about 90 C / 195 F). Pour 120 ml over 1 chamomile tea bag (the page uses 4 to 5 bags per quart) and steep 7 to 10 minutes.
While the tea is still warm, stir in 3/4 to 1 tbsp honey until fully dissolved.
Stir in about 1/4 tsp lemon juice.
Add 120 ml cold water, pour into a glass or small carafe and refrigerate until cold.
Pour over ice. For a fizzy version, add a splash of sparkling water.
garnish: fresh lavender or a slice of green apple (optional)
verified_note: Page makes 1 quart (about 950 ml); divided by 4 for a single glass. Brewed chamomile mapped to chamomile_tea (120 ml hot brew) plus 120 ml cold water. Lemon juice 1/4 tsp is about 1 ml.

name: Masala Shikanji
steps: Roll a large lemon on a hard counter, pressing firmly with your palm, then cut and juice it to get about 30 ml (2 tbsp) juice.

Make the shikanji masala for one glass: mix 1/8 tsp black salt, 1/8 tsp rock salt, 1/3 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/8 tsp black pepper, 1/8 tsp chaat masala and about 1/6 tsp dried mint powder (about 1 tsp in total).
In a glass, stir the 30 ml lemon juice with 2.5 tbsp sugar (or honey) and the 1 tsp masala until the sugar dissolves.
Optional: rim the serving glass by dipping it in lemon juice and then in shikanji masala or brown sugar.
Lightly crush a few mint leaves (about 4) with a mortar and pestle.
Fill a tall glass with ice, add 1 or 2 lemon slices and the crushed mint.
Pour in the lemon base, top with chilled water or chilled soda (about 150 ml), stir well and serve immediately.
verified_note: Source makes 4 glasses; divided by 4 (1/2 cup lemon juice, 10 tbsp sugar, 4 tsp masala, amounts for the whole batch). Rock salt and black salt combined into black_salt. Dried mint powder (about 1/6 tsp) folded into fresh mint leaves. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page gives no volume for the top-up water or soda, 150 ml is an estimate to fill a tall glass. The page's note that the base is only 2-3 tbsp per glass conflicts with its ingredient quantities; the ingredient quantities were used.

name: Nimbu Pani
steps: Squeeze the lemon into cold water
Add sugar, black salt, roasted cumin and chaat masala
Stir until the sugar dissolves, then taste and adjust

name: Jaljeera
steps: Make the jaljeera powder once and keep it (batch): dry-roast 2 tbsp cumin on low heat until aromatic and golden brown, then add 2 tsp pepper and roast on low until aromatic.

Cool the roasted spices completely and put them in a grinder jar. Add 2 tbsp black salt, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp ginger powder, 2 tbsp amchur (dry mango powder) and 2 tbsp sugar, and grind to a fine powder.
For one glass, grind 1.5 tbsp mint, 1 tbsp coriander leaves and 3/8 tsp of the jaljeera powder to a fine paste.
Put a few ice cubes in a tall glass and pour the paste over them.
Add ice-cold water (or soda) to fill the glass, about 200 ml, and a lemon slice.
Garnish with mint and serve. Skip the ice if you have a cold or sore throat.
verified_note: Page: 3 tbsp mint, 2 tbsp coriander, 3/4 tsp jaljeera powder for 2 servings, divided by 2. 3/8 tsp powder is mostly cumin, black salt and amchur (about 1/12 tsp each), written as pinches; pepper, ginger and sugar in the powder are trace. Page gives no amount for the water or soda; 200 ml is an assumption for a tall glass. Lemon slices mapped to lemon:1pcs.

name: Jeera Pani Soda
steps: Make the pre-mix once (batch): dry-roast 1/4 cup jeera (cumin) and 1 tsp black peppercorns, cool, and grind to a very fine powder.
Mix in 1 tbsp dry ginger powder, 1 tbsp chaat masala and 1 tbsp black salt. Store in a clean dry bottle in the fridge for up to a month.
For one 6 oz (180 ml) glass, put 3/4 tsp of the pre-mix and 1 tsp lime juice in the glass, with ice if you like.
Top with about 170 ml chilled club soda and stir.
verified_note: Page uses 3/4 tsp pre-mix per 180 ml glass; the pre-mix (about 22 tsp total) is 12 tsp cumin, 1 tsp pepper, 3 tsp dry ginger, 3 tsp black salt, 3 tsp chaat masala, so per glass about 0.41 tsp cumin, 0.03 tsp pepper and 0.1 tsp each of the others. Dry ginger powder mapped to ginger. Soda 170 ml fills the glass to 180 ml. Ice optional on the page.

name: Masala Soda
steps: Blend 2 tbsp packed mint leaves, 1/4 tsp chopped ginger, 1/2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 1/4 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3/4 tsp chaat masala, 1/8 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp black salt and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine mesh strainer.
Pour 4 to 5 tbsp of the strained mixture into a tall glass.
Add a few ice cubes.
Top with chilled club soda (about 150 ml), stir gently, garnish with a lime slice and mint leaves, and serve immediately.
verified_note: Source makes 4 glasses from one blended concentrate, divided by 4. A blender will need a larger batch in practice (multiply amounts, use 4-5 tbsp of concentrate per glass). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Club soda is 'as required'; 150 ml is an estimate. Lime juice 2 tbsp / 4 = 0.5 tbsp.

name: Aam Panna
steps: Cook the raw mango in a little water until soft
Blend with sugar or jaggery and mint, then strain
Stir in cumin, black salt and pepper
Dilute the concentrate with cold water and serve chilled

name: Kokum Sharbat
steps: Put the kokum concentrate (kokum cooked with sugar, cumin, cardamom and black salt) in a glass
Top with chilled water or soda
Add a few ice cubes and garnish with mint

name: Sol Kadhi
steps: Rinse 2 dried kokum lightly, place in a bowl with about 40 ml (3 tbsp) water and soak for 30 minutes.
Crush and squeeze the kokum in the water with your fingers, then strain, pressing the shreds with a spoon to extract all the flavor.
Add about 80 ml (1/3 cup) water to the kokum extract, then stir in about 50 ml (3 tbsp) thick coconut milk and salt to taste.
For the tempering, heat about 1/4 tsp neutral oil in a small pan on low heat. Add a pinch of mustard seeds and let them crackle, then a pinch of cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add 1 to 2 curry leaves, a small piece of dry Kashmiri chili (seeds removed), half a small crushed garlic clove and a pinch of asafoetida. Fry, stirring often, until the garlic is light golden.
Quickly pour the tempering over the kokum and coconut milk mixture and mix well. Stir in 1 tsp chopped coriander.
Serve right away, or chill for a few hours, in a small glass or bowl. Do not leave it at room temperature as the coconut milk can turn rancid. Garnish with coriander.
verified_note: Page gives no servings; whole batch is 12 kokum, 3 cups water, 1 to 1.5 cups thick coconut milk and I divided by 6 to get a small glass of about 170 ml (my assumption). Salt is 'as required'. Tempering uses mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, chili, garlic, hing mapped approximately; oil and curry leaves are not mapped. Not included: neutral oil (about 1/4 tsp), curry leaves (1 to 2)

name: Rooh Afza Sharbat
steps: Soak the sabja seeds in water for 30 minutes and drain
Stir the Rooh Afza syrup into cold water
Add the soaked seeds and ice, and stir well

name: Mango Cardamom Lassi
steps: Add 1/2 cup (120 g) canned sweetened mango pulp (or 3/4 cup / 140 g chopped ripe sweet mango, chilled, peeled and cubed), 3/8 cup (88 g) cold plain yogurt, 90 ml (3/8 cup) cold milk, 3/4 to 1.5 tbsp sugar and 1/8 tsp cardamom powder to a blender jar.
Blend until super smooth; the texture should be thick but still pourable.
Taste and adjust: add more sugar for sweetness, or more milk or ice to thin it.
Pour into a glass. For a colder drink refrigerate for 1 hour.
Garnish with a few sliced pistachios or a pinch of saffron (optional).
verified_note: Page uses 1.5 cups (280 g) chopped mango or 1 cup (240 g) canned pulp for 2 servings. Sugar (18-36 g for 2) mapped to simple_syrup at 1 tbsp; cardamom powder is marked optional on the page. Page says milk may be replaced with water or ice.

name: Sweet Lassi
steps: Blend chilled yogurt, sugar, cardamom and rose water
Add chilled water and blend until smooth and frothy

name: Rose Cardamom Lassi
steps: Add 1 cup (240 ml) plain yogurt to a blender jar.
Add 1/4 tsp ground cardamom, a small pinch of salt (1/16 tsp), 1 tbsp rose syrup, 1/2 tbsp sugar and 3 ice cubes.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour into a glass, garnish with 1/2 tsp edible dried rose petals and serve.
verified_note: Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (0.5tbsp); salt mapped to black_salt; ice omitted.

name: Salted Mint Lassi
steps: Blend 1/8 cup mint leaves with 1 tbsp of the yogurt to a paste.
Add the remaining yogurt (about 1 cup total), 1/2 tsp ginger juice, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp black salt and 1/2 cup (120 ml) water.
Blend until just smooth; stop there since over-blending makes it frothy.
Pour over 1/4 cup ice cubes, sprinkle with a little roasted cumin powder (1/16 tsp) and a few mint leaves and serve.
garnish: mint leaves and roasted cumin powder
verified_note: Salt 1/4 tsp plus black salt 1/8 tsp combined into black_salt:0.38tsp. Ginger juice mapped to ginger. Roasted cumin powder 1/16 tsp.

name: Cardamom Banana Lassi
steps: Blend 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 1 ripe peeled banana, a splash of cold milk and a handful of ice cubes until smooth. Add sugar to taste only if needed.
Pour into a tumbler and sprinkle with cardamom powder.
verified_note: Source makes 2 (2 bananas, 4 tbsp Greek yoghurt), halved. 'Splash of cold milk', ice and sugar have no amounts on the page so milk and sugar left out of ings. 'Sprinkle of cardamom' mapped to 1 pinch. Greek yoghurt mapped to yogurt.

name: Melon Lassi
steps: Blend 1/8 of a melon (chopped, about 100 g), 1 tbsp Greek yoghurt and 1/2 tsp sugar (or to taste) until smooth.
Crush some ice and put it in a tumbler.
Pour the blended mixture over the ice.
verified_note: Source makes 4 from 1/2 melon, 4 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp sugar; divided by 4. Melon type is not specified and no id for it exists; mapped to watermelon, with the 100 g weight an estimate for 1/8 of a melon. Greek yoghurt mapped to yogurt. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Total is small (about 125 ml before ice).

name: Strawberry Lassi
steps: Rinse, hull and roughly chop about 165 g strawberries (page uses 325 to 350 g for 2).
Blend the strawberries with 3 tbsp sugar or honey into a smooth puree.
Add about 3/4 cup (150 ml) full fat chilled yogurt, 1 to 1.5 tbsp cream (25 to 30% fat) and 1/2 to 1 tsp rose water, then pulse at intervals until smooth and creamy.
Serve right away, garnished with sliced strawberry or mint leaves. Ice cubes can be added when serving.
verified_note: Page serves 1 to 2; divided by 2 using midpoints (sugar 6 to 7 tbsp, rose water 1 to 2 tsp, cream 2 to 3 tbsp, curd 1 to 1.5 cups, strawberries 325 to 350 g). Sugar or honey mapped to simple_syrup. Page names no glass.

name: Mango Coconut Passionfruit Lassi (Dairy-Free)
steps: Put 1/2 cup (120 ml) dairy-free coconut yogurt, 1/2 cup mango pieces, the pulp and seeds of half a passion fruit (about 10 ml) and 1 tbsp (15 ml) vegan milk or water into a blender.
Add a little ice if you like (optional) and blend until smooth. Adjust thickness with more water or dairy-free milk.
Serve chilled.
verified_note: Coconut yogurt mapped to coconut_milk (closest id). Mango pieces mapped to mango_pulp by volume (1/2 cup). Half a passion fruit pulp estimated as about 10 ml puree. 1/4 cup vegan milk or water divided by 4 = about 1 tbsp (15 ml), mapped to water. Page names no glass.

name: Kefir Mango Lassi
steps: Blend about 1/4 cup very ripe cubed (or frozen) mango with 3/8 cup plain milk kefir.
Taste and add honey (about 3/4 tsp) if you want it sweeter.
If using fresh mango, blend in 1 ice cube for a colder drink, or serve over whole ice cubes.
Add a tiny pinch of cayenne pepper if you like and drink immediately.
verified_note: Page serves 4 (or 2 large) from 1 mango, 1.5 cups kefir, 1 tbsp honey; divided by 4. Kefir mapped to yogurt. Mango cubes mapped to mango_pulp. Cayenne and ice optional and omitted from ings.

name: Masala Chaas
steps: Put 1/2 cup (120 ml) plain yogurt, 1 cup (240 ml) cold water, 1/2 green chili, a 1/4 inch piece of ginger, 1/2 tbsp chopped cilantro, 1/4 tsp cumin powder, 1/4 tsp black salt (kala namak), 1/8 tsp regular salt and 1/8 tsp chaat masala into a blender.
Blend until combined.
Pour into a glass, garnish with fresh cilantro or mint, and serve well chilled.
verified_note: Source makes 2; halved. Green chili mapped to chili (0.5 pcs). Ginger 'inch' mapped to pcs (a 1/4 inch piece). Black salt plus regular salt combined into black_salt (0.25 + 0.125 tsp). Page says only 'serving glasses'. Total is about 360 ml.

name: Soda Chaas
steps: Whisk 1/4 cup (60 ml) plain yogurt and 2 tbsp (30 ml) water together in a jug or glass.
Add salt to taste (a pinch), 1/2 tsp crushed roasted cumin seeds and 1/8 tsp ground black pepper, and mix well.
Pour the yogurt mixture into a glass.
Top with 1 cup (240 ml) chilled sparkling or soda water.
Sprinkle 1/2 tbsp each of finely chopped mint and coriander on top and serve immediately.
verified_note: Halved from 2 servings. 'Salt, to taste' mapped to a pinch of black_salt. Page names no glass type.

name: Piyush
steps: Put 100 g (about 1/2 cup) shrikhand, 3/4 cup (about 180 ml) fresh curd, 90 to 120 ml (about 6 to 8 tbsp) cold milk, 1 to 1.5 tbsp sugar, 1 to 1.5 green cardamoms ground to a fine powder and 1/8 tsp nutmeg in a bowl.
Blend until smooth and creamy with a hand blender, whisk or madani churner.
Optionally crush a pinch of saffron and add it while blending for a light yellow colour.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours (skip if all ingredients were cold). Taste and add sugar if needed.
Pour into a glass, top with 3 to 4 sliced pistachios and a few saffron strands, and serve.
verified_note: Shrikhand has no id; merged into yogurt (100 g shrikhand + 180 ml curd = yogurt:280). Shrikhand is already sweet, sugar kept at page amount. Halved from 2 servings.

name: Thandai
steps: Soak for 1 to 2 hours in 2 tbsp (30 ml) warm water: about 1.5 tsp almonds, 1 tsp pistachios, 1/4 tbsp white poppy seeds (khus khus), 1.5 tsp melon seeds (about 10 g nuts and seeds in all), 1/4 tbsp rose petals, 3/8 tsp fennel seeds and a tiny pinch (about 1/16 tsp) of whole black pepper. Or soak overnight in the fridge.
Blend the soaked mixture with its soaking water, about 1/2 of one green cardamom (seeds only), 2 saffron strands and 1 tbsp (12 g) sugar to a very smooth paste (about 4 tbsp).
Stir the 4 tbsp paste into 1 cup (240 ml) cold milk. Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Add a few ice cubes if you like. Garnish with rose petals and chopped almonds or pistachios and serve right away.
garnish: rose petals, chopped almonds or pistachios
verified_note: Page makes 8 to 9 glasses with 8 cups milk; divided by 8. Almonds + pistachios + melon seeds = about 10 g mapped to nuts. Sugar 12 g mapped to simple_syrup:12g. 15-18 saffron strands /8 = about 2 strands = 1 pinch. White poppy seeds have no id. Not included: white poppy seeds (khus khus) 0.25tbsp

name: Mango Thandai
steps: Put 3/8 cup (90 ml) mango pulp, 1/2 cup diced sweet mango, 1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk (or milk of choice), 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp thandai powder, 1 pinch saffron and 1/4 cup ice cubes into a blender.
Blend until creamy and smooth. The page suggests running the smoothie setting twice to bring out the thandai flavour.
Optional: strain through a mesh strainer or cheesecloth.
Pour into a glass, garnish with 1 tbsp diced mango and a pinch of saffron, and serve chilled.
verified_note: Source: 3/4 cup mango pulp plus 1 cup diced mango for 2; halved to 90 ml pulp plus 1/2 cup (about 80 ml) diced mango, combined as mango_pulp:170. Thandai powder (a nut, seed and spice blend, no ingredient list on the page) mapped to nuts:2tbsp. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Saffron halved is under a pinch, kept as 1 pinch. Page names no glass.

name: Mango Mastani
steps: Peel half a very large mango (about 100 ml pulp) and remove the pulp.
Blend the mango with 60 ml (1/4 cup) chilled whole milk, 1 or 2 ice cubes, 1/2 tbsp sugar and a pinch (about 1/16 tsp) of cardamom powder until smooth.
Pour the shake into a glass, filling it about 3/4 full to leave room for the ice cream.
Top with 1 scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Garnish with about 1/2 tbsp chopped nuts (cashews, almonds, pistachios), 1/2 tbsp tutti frutti, a few mango pieces and a glazed cherry.
Serve immediately with a spoon and straw.
garnish: chopped nuts, tutti frutti, mango pieces, glazed cherry
verified_note: Source makes 2 very large servings (or 4 smaller); divided by 4 to keep under 450 ml. 2 very large mangoes / 4 = half a mango, pulp estimated at about 100 ml. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. 1 scoop ice cream = ice_cream:1pcs. Nuts 0.5 tbsp mapped to about 8 g. Tutti frutti and cherry have no id (garnish only). Ice not counted.

name: Rose Falooda
steps: Soak 1.5 tsp sweet basil seeds (sabja) in 1/4 cup water; they swell into a gel within minutes.
Boil water, cut 1/4 pack of falooda sev (thin corn noodles) into 2 to 3 inch pieces and cook per the package directions. Drain, rinse in cold water and drain well.
In a tall glass layer 2 tbsp soaked basil seeds, 2 tbsp cooked noodles and 2 tbsp rose syrup.
Pour in 2/3 cup (about 160 ml) cold milk and top with 1 scoop vanilla ice cream.
Add sliced pistachios and dried rose petals if you like, stir gently, add more rose syrup to taste and serve immediately.
garnish: sliced pistachios, edible dried rose petals
verified_note: Falooda sev amount is a fraction of a pack (0.25pcs = 1/4 pack, pack size not given). Ice cream is 1 scoop. Soaking water omitted.

name: Badam Milk
steps: Rinse about 12 almonds and soak them in 2 tbsp (about 28 ml) hot boiling water, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes.
Drain the water and peel the almonds by pressing the skins off.
Add the peeled almonds, 1 1/3 tbsp sugar, the seeds of 1 green cardamom and a tiny pinch of saffron to a grinder jar. Add about 25 ml milk and grind until completely smooth.
Pour the paste into a saucepan. Swirl about 40 ml milk in the grinder jar to collect the leftover paste and pour that in too.
Add the remaining milk (about 120 ml) and mix well.
Heat on a low flame, stirring often so it does not scorch; a light boil is fine. Switch off once the milk is hot.
Serve hot or warm, or chill it first. Optionally garnish with rose petals, sliced blanched almonds or a few saffron strands.
verified_note: Source (35 almonds, 2.25 cups milk, 4 tbsp sugar, 4 cardamoms, light pinch saffron, 1 cup = 250 ml) divided by 3. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Kesar Milk (Saffron Milk)
steps: Soak 6 to 7 strands of saffron in about 2 tsp of the milk (taken from the 250 ml), refrigerated, for 2 hours.
Heat the rest of the milk over medium heat, stirring often so it does not scorch.
When the milk boils, add the soaked saffron, about 3 slivered almonds, 3 cashews, 3 pistachios and 1 chopped seedless date. Stir well.
Reduce to low heat and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add 1 tsp sugar and cook 2 to 3 more minutes, stirring frequently. Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Remove from heat and serve hot in a glass, or chill 3 to 4 hours. Garnish with slivered nuts and dried rose petals.
garnish: slivered nuts and dried rose petals
verified_note: Page serves 4 from 1 litre; divided by 4. Mixed almonds, cashews and pistachios mapped to nuts (3+3+3 pcs). Dates mapped to dried_fruit. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Optional poppy seeds and chironji left unmapped. Not included: white poppy seeds (0.25 tsp, optional), chironji (0.25 tsp)

name: Masala Doodh
steps: Dry-roast 3 almonds, 3 cashews, 4 pistachios and 1 cardamom pod on low heat for 1 to 3 minutes until fragrant, then turn off the heat and stir in 4 saffron strands
Let the mix cool completely, then pulse it in a grinder to a coarse or fine powder (make extra and keep it in an airtight box in the fridge)
Bring 1 cup full-cream milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-low heat, stirring now and then so it does not stick
Stir in the nut and spice powder, a pinch of grated nutmeg, a tiny pinch of turmeric and 1 tablespoon sugar, and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes until slightly thick and fragrant
Serve warm or chilled, topped with chopped pistachios, almonds and a few saffron strands
garnish: chopped pistachios and almonds, saffron strands

name: Saffron Cardamom Horchata
steps: Rinse 1 1/3 tbsp long grain rice under cold water, then soak it with 1 cardamom pod in about 40 ml water for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Blend the soaked rice, its water and the cardamom until smooth.
Strain through cheesecloth and discard the rice.
Whisk in 20 ml condensed milk, 40 ml whole milk, 20 ml almond milk and 2 pinches (about 2 strands) saffron.
Add a little extra cardamom powder if you like, pour into a glass over ice and top with more saffron.
verified_note: Source makes 6 so amounts divided by 6; saffron is 10-12 strands total, about 2 strands per serving. Total liquid is small (about 120 ml) before ice.

name: Watermelon Juice (Tarbooz)
steps: Add 2/3 cup watermelon cubes, 2/3 tbsp mint leaves, 2/3 tbsp lemon juice, a small pinch (about 1/12 tsp) pepper powder and 1/3 tbsp sugar to a blender.
Blend well without adding any water.
Pour into a glass and garnish with mint.
verified_note: Page (fresh watermelon juice variation): 2 cups watermelon, 2 tbsp mint, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1 tbsp sugar for 3 servings, divided by 3. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Yield is small (about 120 ml).

name: Fresh Pomegranate Juice
steps: Pulse arils briefly and strain
Add a dash of lemon and salt

name: Fresh Pineapple Juice
steps: Peel a quarter of a medium pineapple, cutting off the skin and eyes, then chop it into 1-inch pieces.
Add the pineapple pieces, 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, 0.5 tbsp sugar and a pinch of black salt to a blender. Skip the sugar if the pineapple is very sweet.
Blend until smooth.
Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing the pulp with a spoon to extract all the liquid, and discard the fibrous pulp.
Pour into a glass over a few ice cubes, garnish with mint and a pineapple wedge if you like, and serve immediately.
verified_note: 1/4 of a medium whole pineapple entered as pineapple:0.25pcs (id is pineapple chunks). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup; black salt 1/4 tsp divided by 4 is about a pinch.

name: Mint & Clove Ginger Beer (Homemade)
steps: Wash, peel and roughly chop 15 g fresh ginger.
Add the ginger, 2 tbsp fresh mint and 1/4 cup muscovado sugar (or sweetener of choice) to a blender. If using whole cloves, add them now.
Add a little water and blend until smooth.
Strain through a sieve or cheesecloth to get the juice.
Stir in 2 tbsp (30 ml) lemon or lime juice and 1/8 tsp clove powder. The syrup can be refrigerated for later.
Add ice to a mug, pour in the syrup about a third of the way up, and top with chilled sparkling water (about 1 cup, 240 ml) to fill about two-thirds of the glass.
Garnish with lime or lemon slices and mint, and serve immediately.
verified_note: Source makes 2 in beer mugs; halved. Muscovado sugar mapped to simple_syrup (0.25 cup). Water for blending is 'a little', no amount given, omitted. Ginger given in grams, kept as g. Page says juice is lemon or lime; mapped to lime_juice.

name: Fiery Ginger Beer Bug
steps: Make the ginger bug first (this is a starter, not scaled): in a clean jar stir 50 g finely grated fresh ginger, 50 g sugar and 500 ml water, cover with a cloth held with a rubber band. Each day for days 2 to 5 stir in 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tbsp sugar. It is ready when bubbles form, usually after 3 to 5 days.
For one serving of ginger beer (1/10 of the batch): in a pot combine 10 g grated ginger, 15 g brown or coconut sugar and 50 ml water. Boil, then simmer about 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat, add 150 ml more water and let cool to room temperature.
Pour into a clean bottle leaving headspace, add about 8 ml lemon juice (1/5 of a lemon) and 12 ml strained ginger bug liquid. Seal tightly and leave at room temperature for 2 to 3 days.
Strain into a small bottle (250 to 500 ml) with a lid, seal and leave at room temperature for 2 to 3 more days, releasing the pressure daily so it does not overflow.
Check daily; when the bottle feels firm, open briefly to release pressure and reseal. If very fizzy, refrigerate to slow fermentation.
Chill and serve over ice.
verified_note: Divided by 10 (100 g ginger, 150 g sugar, juice of 2 lemons, 2 litres water). Water 200 ml is the 2 L batch /10 including the 50 ml used to simmer. Brown or coconut sugar mapped to simple_syrup in grams. Ginger bug liquid (12 ml per serving) has no id. Page includes a multi-day fermentation, not a quick mix. Not included: ginger bug liquid (fermented starter), 12 ml

name: Spiced Apple Cider Sparkler
glass: spritz glass or large bell wine glass
steps: Chill all ingredients first so no ice is needed.
Add 4 oz (120 ml) apple cider, 1 oz (30 ml) lemon juice and 1/2 oz (15 ml) cinnamon syrup (or a pinch of powdered cinnamon) to a spritz glass or large bell wine glass.
Top with 2 to 3 oz (60 to 90 ml) non-alcoholic sparkling wine.
Stir gently to combine.
Garnish with apple slices, a cinnamon stick and star anise.
garnish: apple slices, cinnamon stick, star anise
verified_note: Cinnamon syrup mapped to simple_syrup plus a pinch of cinnamon. Non-alcoholic sparkling wine mapped to sparkling_cider (page also allows sparkling cider, grape juice or ginger ale); used 75 ml.

name: Tamarind Chili Salt Cooler
steps: Make the tamarind base (page batch for 7 drinks: 2 cups water, 3 1/2 tablespoons tamarind chutney, 1/2 teaspoon fennel seeds, 1/2 teaspoon kala namak, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1 inch grated ginger). Whisk everything in a pan over medium heat and bring to a gentle boil, then turn off the heat, cover and steep 30 to 45 minutes.
Strain the liquid and chill it. It keeps 2 to 3 days.

On a plate mix 1 teaspoon kala namak with 1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder (use 1/4 teaspoon chili or skip it for a milder drink). Rub a lime wedge around the rim of a 7 to 8 oz glass and dip it in the spice mix.
Put a lime wedge and 3 to 4 mint leaves in the glass and muddle them.
Fill the glass with ice, add 2 oz (60 ml) of the chilled tamarind liquid and top with about 6 oz (180 ml) Canada Dry Zero until full.
Garnish with more mint and serve immediately.
garnish: mint leaves, lime wedge, black salt and chili rim
verified_note: Different name (Spiced Tamarind Mocktail), closest real match with tamarind, black salt and chili rim. Tamarind chutney mapped to tamarind paste; kala namak to black_salt; Canada Dry Zero to ginger_ale; sugar to simple_syrup. Single-serving amounts for the base are 1/7 of the batch; the full batch is given in step 1.

name: Golden Turmeric Elixir
steps: Put 1/2 tablespoon of finely grated unpeeled fresh turmeric root (or about 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon ground turmeric) and 1/4 teaspoon finely grated fresh ginger in a heatproof jar or cup.
Pour in 180 ml (3/4 cup) boiling filtered water and add a tiny pinch of sea salt. Let it steep uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 tablespoon raw honey until it dissolves, then strain into another jar or glass and let it cool to room temperature.
Stir in about 22 ml (1 1/2 tablespoons) fresh lemon juice and 15 ml (1 tablespoon) fresh orange juice. Taste and adjust the honey and citrus to your liking.
Serve at room temperature or chilled in a tall glass. For a hot drink, pour about 2 tablespoons of the finished drink into a mug and top it with boiling water.
verified_note: Page is Turmeric Lemonade (4 servings), closest real match to a turmeric-ginger-lemon-honey elixir. Fresh turmeric mapped to turmeric; orange juice added by the page. Page has no coconut water, black pepper, or shaking.

name: Pineapple Jalapeño Smash
steps: Make the jalapeño simple syrup ahead: combine 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup sugar and 1 sliced jalapeño in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, remove from heat and let cool. (This makes extra; you need 1/4 cup per drink.)
Fill a small cocktail glass about two-thirds full with ice.
Add 120 ml (1/2 cup) pineapple juice and 60 ml (1/4 cup) jalapeño simple syrup and stir to combine.
Top with about 60 ml (1/4 cup) seltzer, or to taste.
Garnish with jalapeño slices and a pineapple wedge.
verified_note: Jalapeño infused in the syrup mapped to chili (about 1/3 of a jalapeño per drink); syrup mapped to simple_syrup; seltzer to soda_water.

name: Smoked Orange & Cardamom Fizz
steps: Char orange halves and juice them
Shake with cardamom syrup and lemon
Strain and top with tonic

name: Cranberry Rosemary Shrub
steps: Make the shrub ahead (these are 1/6 of the page's batch): put 1/4 cup fresh cranberries, about 2 tbsp orange slices or segments, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 1 to 1 1/2 tbsp plus 2 tsp granulated sugar (1/10 cup), a small piece of cinnamon stick and 1/3 of a sprig of rosemary in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high, then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes, until the fruit breaks down, stirring and gently muddling as it simmers.
Taste and add sugar or vinegar to suit your preference.
Cool completely, then strain through a fine-mesh strainer into a jar and discard the cinnamon and rosemary. Leftover shrub keeps 3 to 4 weeks airtight.
To serve, fill a glass halfway with ice, add about 2 tablespoons of the shrub and top with seltzer, tonic, soda or carbonated water.
verified_note: Page makes shrub for 6 drinks and uses about 2 tbsp shrub per drink, so ings are 1/6 of the batch. Cranberries mapped to berries (fresh cranberries). Sugar range 1/2 to 2/3 cup divided by 6 about 0.1 cup, mapped to simple_syrup. Page gives no amount for the soda ('top with'); soda_water:150 is an estimate to fill a glass. Rosemary 2 sprigs /6 = 0.33, cinnamon 1 stick /6 = 0.17.

name: Blood Orange Ginger Elixir
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Add 2 oz (60 ml) blood orange juice (about 1 blood orange) and 1 oz (30 ml) lime juice, then stir to combine.
Top with 4 oz (120 ml) ginger beer or ginger ale.
Garnish with citrus slices or fresh mint if desired.
verified_note: Blood orange juice mapped to orange_juice. Ginger beer or ginger ale both allowed by the page; ginger_beer used.

name: Kadha (Immunity Brew)
steps: Put 360 ml (1 1/2 cups) water in a saucepan over medium-high heat.
Coarsely crush 2 black peppercorns and 2 cloves with a mortar and pestle and add them to the water.
Add 1 teaspoon grated ginger, 1 pinch ground turmeric, and (optional) 1/2 tablespoon lemongrass leaves. Boil until the liquid reduces by half, about 15 minutes.
Add 1 teaspoon jaggery (or honey or other sweetener, optional) and cook about 2 more minutes until it melts.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Halved from 2 servings. Lemongrass and jaggery are optional on the page. Water amount is before reducing by half.

name: Golden Milk (Haldi Doodh)
steps: Add 1 cup (250 ml) milk to a saucepan over medium heat and bring it to a low boil.
Add 3/4 tsp ground turmeric, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground cardamom (optional), 1/8 tsp ground black pepper and 1/2 tbsp (1 1/2 tsp) chopped or grated fresh ginger.
Stir well and bring to a boil, then simmer for 7 to 8 minutes, until fragrant.
Add a tiny pinch (1/8 tsp) of ghee or coconut oil and mix well.
Turn off the heat and sweeten to taste with honey, maple syrup, sugar or jaggery, if desired.
Strain through a fine strainer into a mug, sprinkle with a little ground cinnamon and drink warm before bedtime.
verified_note: Page serves 2 to 3 with 2 cups (500 ml) milk; halved to 1 cup assuming 2 servings. Turmeric is ground (1/2 tbsp, halved to 3/4 tsp); ginger is fresh, 1 tbsp halved. Page gives no sweetener amount ('to taste'), so none listed. Not included: ghee or coconut oil, 1/8 tsp

name: Homemade Electrolyte Drink
steps: Grate a 1 inch piece of ginger and squeeze its juice through a mesh strainer into a bowl or jar.
Add 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1/2 to 1 tablespoon honey, and 1/8 teaspoon pink Himalayan salt to the ginger juice. Whisk until combined.
Stir in 1 cup (240 ml) water, mineral water or sparkling water.
Pour over ice in a cup. You can also refrigerate it for 1 to 2 days instead.
verified_note: Used the page's Lemon Ginger version (2 servings, halved). Pink Himalayan salt mapped to black_salt. 1 inch ginger = 1pcs. Page offers mineral or sparkling water; used plain water. Honey given as 1 to 2 tbsp per 2 servings, so 0.75 tbsp used.

name: Easy Mulled Apple Cider
steps: Combine 1 cup fresh apple cider or unfiltered apple juice, 1/2 cinnamon stick, 2/3 of a clove (about 1 clove is fine), a pinch of star anise (optional) and 2 orange slices in a small saucepan (a lemon slice is optional).
Heat over medium-high until it just starts to bubble. Do not let it boil hard.
Cover and keep at a very low simmer for 30 minutes.
Taste. If you want it sweeter, stir in 1 tsp brown sugar or maple syrup, then taste again and repeat until sweet enough.
Ladle into a mug and garnish with an orange slice and a star anise.
verified_note: Divided by 6 (6 cups cider, 3 cinnamon sticks, 4 cloves, 2 star anise, 1 sliced orange). orange:2pcs means 2 slices (no slice unit). Star anise shares the clove id, covered by clove:0.67pcs and mentioned in steps. Sweetener (1/4 cup brown sugar or maple syrup per batch) is optional and added to taste, so not in ings. Page has no ginger.

name: Apple Cider Vinegar Morning Tonic
steps: In a mug or glass, combine 1 cup warm water (comfortably warm, not boiling), 2 tbsp raw apple cider vinegar and 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about half a lemon), then stir well.
Add 1 tsp raw honey or maple syrup, 1/4 tsp ground ginger (or 1/2 inch fresh ginger, grated) and a pinch of ground cinnamon.
Stir until the honey has fully dissolved (fresh ginger needs a little more stirring).
Taste and adjust sweetness or spice; a tiny pinch of cayenne is optional.
Drink right away, ideally 15 to 20 minutes before your first meal of the day.
verified_note: Ginger given as 1/4 tsp ground (ginger id is fresh ginger, so this is the ground amount). Honey or maple syrup either works; honey used. Water is warm, so temp set to hot (warm).

name: On The Mend Hot Toddy (Zero-Proof)
steps: Heat 330 ml (11.6 fl oz) non-alcoholic apple cider in the microwave or in a pan on the stove. Do not heat it in the mug.
Pour hot water into your glass or mug and swirl it to warm the vessel, then discard the water.
Pour the warm cider into the warmed mug.
Stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 4 slices of fresh ginger root.
Taste and adjust, adding more lemon or ginger for balance.
verified_note: No page exists for this exact name; used a real non-alcoholic hot toddy recipe. Ginger slices mapped as ginger pcs. Non-alcoholic apple cider mapped to apple_juice.

name: Caramelized Apple Crisp Mocktail
steps: Spread a thin layer of caramel sauce on a small plate, and on a second plate mix crushed cookies with cinnamon.
Dip the rim of a coupe or martini glass in the caramel, then coat it in the cookie and cinnamon mixture.
In a mixing glass, combine 1.5 oz (45 ml) orange juice, 3 oz (90 ml) unsweetened apple cider, 1/4 tsp rum extract, 2 dashes caramel sauce and 1 cup of ice.
Stir well with a cocktail spoon until chilled.
Strain into the prepared glass, garnish with apple slices and serve immediately.
garnish: sliced apple, caramel and crushed cookie-cinnamon rim
verified_note: Closest published match to the name (apple crisp + caramel); page title is Apple Crisp Caramel Mocktini. Unsweetened apple cider mapped to apple_juice. Page uses Torani zero calorie caramel sauce; mapped to caramel_syrup. Ice not listed as ingredient. Not included: rum extract 1/4 tsp, crushed cookies for rim

name: Virgin Black Forest Cherry Fizz
steps: Rim the glass: brush the outside rim with chocolate spread, spray 2 tbsp cacao nibs with edible gold spray and mix until gold, spread them in a shallow dish, and roll the rim in them. Set the glass aside.
In a cocktail shaker (or empty jar) combine 1 tbsp black cherry conserve, 1 tbsp chocolate spread, 100 ml cold sour cherry juice and 2 ice cubes. Seal and shake vigorously until blended.
Strain through a fine sieve into the glass, pouring gently so the rim stays intact.
Top up with about 30 ml cold soda water.
Cut a slit in a cherry (fresh or maraschino) and perch it on the rim.
garnish: cherry with stem, gold cacao nib rim
verified_note: Chocolate spread mapped to chocolate_syrup (1 tbsp in drink; extra 1 tbsp for the rim). Sour cherry juice mapped to cherry_juice. Whipped cream is not on the page. Not included: black cherry conserve 1 tbsp, cacao nibs 2 tbsp and edible gold spray (rim)

name: Orange Blossom Honey Spritz
steps: Make honey syrup by stirring equal parts warm water and honey together, then let it cool. You need 1/2 oz (15 ml) of it, which is 7.5 ml honey and 7.5 ml water.
Build in a highball glass: 1/2 oz honey syrup, 2 dashes orange blossom water, 1/4 oz (7.5 ml) lemon juice and 3 oz (90 ml) club soda.
Add ice and stir gently.
Garnish with a blood orange slice.
verified_note: Closest published match to the name. Page lists no non-alcoholic spirit in its ingredients (confirmed with a second fetch), though it is a Seedlip page. Orange blossom water mapped to rose_water. Club soda mapped to soda_water. Honey syrup split into honey and water 1:1. Total is only about 112 ml.

name: Cranberry Cinnamon Spice Toddy (Chilled)
steps: Pour about 30 ml boiling water over 1/4 of a Tetley Original tea bag and steep for 5 minutes (the page does this in a slow cooker with 2 tea bags and 1 cup boiling water, lid on).
Add 1 cup (240 ml) cranberry juice, 2 tsp sugar, 1 orange slice, about 2/5 of a cinnamon stick and a pinch of ground cloves, and stir well.
Heat gently (the page cooks the batch on low for 2-3 hours or high for 1-2 hours).
Remove the orange slice and cinnamon stick.
Optional: wet the outer rim of the glass with a lemon wedge and dip in super-fine sugar.
Pour the spiced tea into the glass and serve hot, immediately.
verified_note: Page batch is 2 tea bags, 1 cup water, 8 cups cranberry juice, 1/4 cup sugar, 1 orange, 3 cinnamon sticks, 1/2 tsp ground cloves; I divided by 8 as an assumed serving count because the page states none. Original is HOT (rum optional, omitted).

name: Billionaire's Hot Chocolate
steps: Put 3 tbsp shortbread crumbs in a serving mug and press them down with a spoon.
Pour 3 tbsp caramel over the crumbs and let it sit for 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat 3/4 cup (180 ml) full-fat milk in a saucepan over medium heat until it boils.
Add 2 tbsp hot chocolate powder or grated chocolate flakes to the milk and mix well.
Pour the hot chocolate over the set caramel in the mug.
Quickly top with 2 tbsp whipped cream, then sprinkle with 1/2 tsp shortbread crumbs and 1 tsp chocolate shavings (both optional). Serve immediately.
verified_note: Hot chocolate powder or grated chocolate mapped to chocolate_syrup (tbsp). 3/4 cup milk = 180 ml. Not included: shortbread crumbs 3 tbsp (base layer) plus 1/2 tsp for topping

name: Classic Hot Chocolate
steps: Stir sugar, cocoa and a splash of milk over medium heat until it boils, then cook 2 minutes
Take off the heat, add the rest of the milk and warm through without boiling
Serve hot with marshmallows

name: Eggless Eggnog
steps: Mix 1 tbsp cornstarch with a little of the milk in a small bowl and set aside.
In a medium saucepan combine the remaining milk (about 118 ml total), 60 ml heavy cream, 16 g (about 1 tbsp) sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, a pinch of cinnamon and a pinch of freshly grated nutmeg.
Stir over medium heat until warm and the sugar dissolves, without boiling.
Add the cornstarch mixture and cook on medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Do not boil.
Remove from heat and let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Pour into a glass, top with whipped cream if you like, and garnish with freshly grated nutmeg and cinnamon.
garnish: grated nutmeg, cinnamon powder, optional whipped cream
verified_note: Divided 4-serving recipe by 4 (2 cups milk = 470 ml, 1 cup cream = 240 ml, 1/3 cup sugar = 65 g, 4 tbsp cornstarch, 2 tsp vanilla, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp cinnamon). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (g); vanilla extract mapped to vanilla_syrup. Rum/brandy optional, skipped. Page says how to split the milk is unclear; step 1 mixing cornstarch with a little milk is my reading. Step 2 mentions salt but gives no amount. Not included: cornstarch 1 tbsp (7.5 g)

name: Butterbeer (Fan Style)
steps: Whip 50 ml double cream until soft peaks form and set it aside.

In a microwave-safe bowl, heat 125 ml butterscotch syrup or toffee sauce with 1/2 tbsp butter (the page says about 15 seconds in the text; the card's time is missing its unit). You can also warm them on the stovetop.
Mix well.
Add the warm butterscotch mixture to your serving cup.
Slowly pour 250 ml chilled cream soda on top and mix.
Spoon the whipped cream on top and serve immediately.

Total about 425 ml, large for one glass but within limit; page also describes a warm version (room-temp cream soda poured over hot syrup). Not included: cream soda (mapped approx. to lemon_lime_soda), butter 1/2 tbsp

name: Rum-Free Horchata Latte
steps: Make a simple syrup: boil equal parts water and sugar until the sugar dissolves, then cool to room temperature (you need 1 tbsp per latte).
Blend 1 tbsp rice and about 2 g cinnamon bark with 60 ml of the water until the rice is broken down into coarse, pebble-like sand.
Add the remaining 60 ml water, stir, cover and let sit at room temperature for 3 hours.
Blend again until the rice and cinnamon are broken down further.
Strain through a very fine sieve or cheesecloth, stir in 1 tbsp simple syrup and chill. Taste once cold and add more syrup if needed. This gives about 120 ml (4 oz) horchata.
Fill a glass with ice, add the 4 oz chilled horchata and 2 oz (60 ml) strong espresso, stir and serve.
verified_note: Page batch: 1 cup rice, 1 oz cinnamon bark, 6 cups water, 3/4 cup simple syrup = about 12 lattes of 4 oz horchata + 2 oz espresso; divided by 12. Cinnamon bark 1 oz /12 about 2 g. Suggest making a full batch in practice since blending 1 tbsp rice is impractical.

name: Coconut Blackberry Smash
steps: Muddle one blackberry in the bottom of a rocks glass, then add crushed ice.
In a cocktail shaker with ice, combine 2 oz Ritual Gin Alternative, 1 oz coconut cream, 3/4 oz fresh lime juice, 1/4 tsp rosewater (optional) and 2 to 3 more blackberries.
Shake, then pour over the crushed ice in the glass.
Top with more crushed ice and blackberries.
verified_note: Coconut cream mapped to coconut_milk. 3-4 blackberries mapped to berries:4pcs (one muddled, rest in shaker/garnish). Rosewater mapped to rose_water. Ice not an ingredient. Page does not give a serving count. Not included: Ritual Gin Alternative 2 oz (60 ml) non-alcoholic gin

name: Cookies & Cream Shake
steps: Add 1 cup vanilla ice cream, 3/8 cup (90 ml) milk (any fat level) and 3 broken-up chocolate sandwich cookies to a blender jar, in that order, and secure the lid.
Blend on low for about 30 seconds, until smooth and uniform.
Serve immediately.
verified_note: Page makes 2 cups with 2 cups ice cream, 3/4 cup milk, 6 cookies; I halved it to a 1-cup shake (assumption, as the page gives no servings). Glass not given on page. Not included: chocolate sandwich cookies, 3

name: Kala Khatta Sharbat
steps: Combine about 62 g washed jamun (Jawa plum), 1.5 tbsp sugar, 0.12 tsp roasted cumin, 0.15 tsp black salt, a pinch of black pepper powder and 250 ml water in a deep pan (this is 1/8 of the page's batch; the page also adds salt to taste).
Place the pan on high heat. Once the water is hot and the jamun has softened slightly, mash the fruit.
Boil for 30 minutes, then strain through a sieve, pressing out as much pulp as possible.
Stir in about 0.5 tsp lemon juice and let the sharbat cool completely.
To serve, fill a glass with ice cubes, a lemon wheel and a few mint leaves, pour in the sharbat and garnish with another lemon wheel and mint leaves.
verified_note: Page makes 1.5 L from 500 g jamun; scaled to 1/8 (about 190 ml after boiling). Fresh jamun in g mapped to jamun id. 3/4 cup sugar mapped to simple_syrup (tbsp). 1/4 lemon juice approximated as about 1 tbsp then scaled. Page's 'salt to taste' not quantified and omitted. Lemon wheel and mint garnish only.

name: Banta / Street Goli Soda
steps: In a blender jar combine about 1 1/3 tbsp sugar, 5 mint leaves, 30 ml fresh lemon juice (about 2/3 of a lemon), 1/3 tsp cumin powder, a pinch of black pepper powder, a pinch of chaat masala, about 1/6 tsp black salt, 1/3 tbsp grated ginger, a tiny pinch of salt and about 20 ml water.
Blend until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is smooth.
Strain the mixture into a glass.
Add a mint leaf, a lemon slice and crushed ice or ice cubes.
Just before serving, top with about 280 ml chilled club soda or plain soda, garnish with mint, sprinkle a little chaat masala and cumin on top, and serve chilled.
garnish: mint leaves, lemon slice, pinch of chaat masala and cumin
verified_note: Page (Nimbu Masala Soda, also called Banta / Goli Soda) says 3-4 cups soda, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup mint, 2 lemons juice, 1 tsp cumin, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/4 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp black salt, 1 tbsp ginger, 2-3 pinches salt, 1/4 cup water for 2-3 glasses; divided by 3, using 3.5 cups soda at 240 ml per cup. Extra salt folded into black_salt.

name: Fuljar Soda (Kerala Spiced Drop Shot)
glass: tall glass plus a shot glass
steps: Add 0.5 tsp chopped green chili (less spicy variety), 0.25 tsp chopped ginger, 4 mint leaves, 0.5 tbsp fresh lime juice, 0.75 tbsp sugar, a tiny pinch of salt and 0.5 tbsp filtered water to a small blender jar.
Blend until smooth.
Pour the puree into a shot glass.
Add 1 tbsp of soaked sabja (basil) seeds to the shot glass and stir.
Fill a tall glass with chilled club soda to about 3/4 full.
Gently drop the shot glass into the soda. It will fizz up, so drink it immediately.

Sabja is inconsistent on the page: ingredient card says 1 tbsp seeds soaked in 1/4 cup water for the whole batch, while the method says 1 tbsp soaked sabja per glass; entered 0.75 tsp dry seeds (1 tbsp / 4) and kept the method wording. Salt 1/8 tsp / 4 is a tiny pinch.

name: Kacha Aam Pudina Fizz
steps: Mix a spice blend of about 0.5 tsp salt, 0.25 tsp chaat masala, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder and 0.2 tsp black salt (the page makes this blend for 4 glasses).
Put 2 tbsp boiled raw mango puree into a glass and add 1 tsp of the spice blend.
Add 2 tsp mint paste, the juice of half a lemon and 2 tbsp sugar syrup.
Add ice cubes, cover the glass with a steel glass and shake well.
Strain into a serving glass, add fresh ice cubes, top with drinking soda and stir.
Garnish with a slice of raw mango and a fresh mint sprig and serve.
garnish: raw mango slice and mint sprig
verified_note: Page serves 4, divided by 4. Spice blend (salt, black salt, chaat masala, cumin) scaled to the 1 tsp per glass the method uses and salt merged into black_salt. Mint paste 2 tsp approximated as 10 mint leaves. Half a lemon approximated as 15 ml lemon juice. Soda amount 'as required', 150 ml assumed. Glass type not given by the page.

name: Imli Ka Amlana (Rajasthani Tamarind Cooler)
steps: Soak a small piece of tamarind (about a quarter of a gooseberry-sized ball per glass) in 2 tbsp hot water for 30 minutes.
Grind the soaked tamarind into a fine paste.
Strain the paste, then add about 215 ml (just under 1 cup) water.
Stir in a pinch of black pepper powder, a pinch of cardamom powder, a pinch of black salt and 1 tbsp powdered sugar.
Mix well and add a few chopped mint leaves.
Serve chilled, with ice cubes if you like.
verified_note: Page serves 3-4: tamarind 'a small gooseberry sized' (no weight given), 4 cups water, 1/4 tsp each black pepper / cardamom / black salt, 1/4 cup powdered sugar; divided by 4. Per serving spices are 1/16 tsp, written as a pinch. Tamarind about 5 ml paste is an estimate of a quarter gooseberry-sized ball. Powdered sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Street-Style Masala Cola
steps: Add 1/4 tsp black salt and 3/4 tsp chaat masala to a tall glass.
Add 2 fresh lime slices and 3 to 4 mint leaves.
Muddle with a muddler to crush the lime and mint and release their juices.
Add 1/2 to 1 cup of ice cubes to the glass.
Pour in 8 oz (240 ml) cola to fill the glass, then stir.
Garnish with one more lime slice and a mint sprig.
verified_note: 8 ounce coke = 240 ml; 2 lime slices mapped to lime:2pcs; ice skipped; page has no lemon juice, roasted cumin.

name: Jeera Masala Soda
steps: Dry roast 2.4 tsp cumin seeds and 0.3 tsp black peppercorns over medium heat until slightly browned, stirring often. Cool for 5 minutes, then grind to a fine powder.
In a nonstick pan, mix the ground spices with 1.6 tbsp sugar, 0.4 tsp black salt, 0.4 tsp chaat masala and 2 tbsp (24 ml) water.
Cook over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until a thick syrup forms. Strain through a fine mesh strainer.
To serve, put 3 to 4 ice cubes in a glass, add 1 tbsp lime juice and 2 tbsp of the jeera syrup (stir the syrup first).
Top with chilled club soda (about 150 ml), stir and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page's syrup batch (1/2 cup cumin, 1 tbsp peppercorns, 1 cup sugar, 4 tsp black salt, 4 tsp chaat masala, 1 cup water) serves 10 with 2 tbsp syrup each, divided by 10. Lime juice 1 tbsp is per glass (confirmed in assembly step). Page gives no soda amount; 150 ml is an assumption. Syrup spices are strained out but listed as used.

name: Pudina Nimbu Sharbat
steps: Blend 1/4 cup mint leaves, 1/8 tsp grated ginger and 1.5 tsp sugar into a coarse mixture (not a smooth paste), adding a little water to help it blend.
In a glass or small pitcher combine the juice of about 1/2 lemon, the mint mixture and about 60 ml ice-cold water. Stir well.
Taste and adjust sweetness with a little more sugar, syrup or honey.
Add the remaining ice-cold water (about 60 ml) and ice cubes.
Garnish with a lemon slice and serve chilled.
verified_note: Divided by 4. Juice of 2 lemons / 4 = 1/2 lemon, about 15 ml. 2 glasses water / 4 = about 120 ml; page does not split water between steps, 50/50 assumed. Page has no glass named.

name: Classic Rose / Rooh Afza Sharbat
steps: Soak 0.5 tsp sabja (sweet basil) seeds in about 3 tbsp water for about 30 minutes until they swell.
Strain out the soaking water and set the seeds aside.
Pour 1 cup (240 ml) cold or room-temperature water into a glass.
Stir in 1 to 1.25 tbsp Rooh Afza syrup, more or less to taste.
Add the soaked sabja seeds.
For a cold drink, add 1 or 2 ice cubes (optional).
Mix well and serve right away, or chill and drink within a few hours.
verified_note: Page gives no serving count; amounts scaled proportionally (3.5 cups water -> 1 cup). Syrup range 4-5 tbsp per 3.5 cups = about 1.1-1.4 tbsp per cup.

name: Khus Sharbat (Vetiver Grass Cooler)
steps: Make the syrup ahead (page batch makes about 1 litre): rinse 60 to 70 g khus roots very well under running water, drain and chop with clean scissors.
Soak the roots in 5 cups (about 1 litre) water at room temperature for 8 to 9 hours or overnight, then strain, squeezing the roots, and keep the liquid.

Stir 4 cups (600 g) raw or white sugar into the liquid, heat until the sugar dissolves, bring to a boil and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until slightly thick and sticky. Strain into a clean sterilized jar, seal, cool and refrigerate; use within 15 to 20 days.
For one glass, mix about 60 ml (a quarter of the glass) khus syrup with about 190 ml room-temperature or chilled water.
Stir well and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page says mix 1/4 or 1/3 part syrup with water; used 1/4 of a 250 ml glass (60 ml syrup, 190 ml water). Syrup itself is homemade from khus roots; mapped to khus_syrup.

name: Nannari Sharbat (Sarsaparilla Root Cooler)
steps: Put a few ice cubes in a serving glass.
Add 3 tablespoons nannari syrup.
Squeeze in the juice of 1/2 lemon.
Add 1 cup (240 ml) water and mix well.
Serve chilled. For a soda version use soda water instead of plain water; shops also use crushed ice.
verified_note: lemon_juice:0.5pcs = juice of half a lemon (no ml given). Page's sarbath section is one glass.

name: Panakam (South Indian Jaggery Tonic)
steps: Put 4 tbsp chopped jaggery in 240 ml (1 cup) water in a bowl and stir well.
Leave it for 30 to 40 minutes until the jaggery dissolves, then strain if there are any impurities.
Add 1 tbsp (15 ml) lemon juice.
Add 1/8 tsp dried ginger powder, a pinch of black pepper powder (about 1/16 tsp), about 1/5 tsp green cardamom powder and a pinch of salt, and mix thoroughly.
Add 2 tulsi (holy basil) leaves if serving as an offering, or chill it in the fridge or add 1 to 2 ice cubes for drinking.
verified_note: Page quantities (1/2 cup jaggery, 2 cups water, 1/4 tsp ginger powder, 1/8 tsp pepper, 1/3-1/2 tsp cardamom, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 4-5 tulsi) were halved because the page does not state servings and 2 cups is too much for one glass. Dried ginger powder mapped to ginger. Salt mapped to black_salt. Optional edible camphor and ice omitted.

name: Bel Ka Sharbat (Wood Apple Tonic)
steps: Wash the wood apple, cut it open and scoop out the pulp (use half a wood apple per glass).
Put the pulp in a bowl and add water equal to twice the volume of the pulp.
Mash the pulp into the water.
Strain through a heavy strainer, pressing the pulp with a spoon to extract all the juice.
Stir in 1 big tablespoon sugar until fully dissolved.
Add cold water or ice cubes to fill the glass.
If you like, add a pinch of salt and some roasted cumin powder to taste.
verified_note: Page gives no amounts for cumin (optional, to taste) or for the cold water at the end; cumin omitted from ings and 200 ml water used only to fill a glass. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup (id covers sugar). Page does not name a glass. Not included: wood apple (bel) pulp, 0.5 fruit per glass (2 fruits make 4-5 glasses)

name: Namkeen Sattu Sharbat (Savory Gram Cooler)
steps: Put 2 tablespoons sattu in a mug or glass.
Add 1/4 teaspoon roasted cumin powder, 1.5 teaspoons lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon black salt and optionally a small pinch (1/8 teaspoon) black pepper.
Pour in 375 ml chilled water and stir well with a spoon, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in 1 teaspoon each chopped mint and coriander leaves (finely chopped onion or green chilli can also be added).
Serve in a glass, or refrigerate and serve later.
verified_note: Original 4 tbsp sattu, 750 ml water, etc. for 2; halved. Black pepper optional.

name: Meetha Sattu Sharbat (Sweet Roasted Gram)
steps: Pour 350 ml cold or room temperature water into a glass.
Add 1.5 tbsp sattu (roasted black chickpea flour); use a little more for a thicker drink.
Add about 1 tbsp sugar, raw sugar or jaggery, adjusting to taste, and a pinch of black salt (optional). Lemon or lime juice can be added for tang.
Stir well, breaking up any lumps with a spoon.
Serve right away, chilled or over ice, and stir again before drinking because the flour settles.
verified_note: Source makes 3 servings from 1.5 L water (500 ml each) with 2 tbsp sattu per glass, over our 450 ml limit, so the glass was scaled to 350 ml with the sattu and sweetener reduced in the same proportion. The page's method (2-3 tsp sweetener per glass) conflicts with its ingredient list (4-6 tbsp for 3); the list lower bound (about 1.3 tbsp per 500 ml) was scaled. Page gives no cardamom.

name: Gond Katira Rose Cooler
steps: Soak the gond katira in water overnight. In the morning, rinse it and fluff it up to get a translucent jelly texture. Measure out 1 tbsp of the soaked gond.
In a glass, add the 1 tbsp soaked gond katira and 1 tbsp rose water (or gulkand syrup).
Pour 200 ml chilled milk (or almond or coconut milk) over the mixture, stir gently and serve.
verified_note: Page says 'Rose water or Gulkand syrup'; mapped to rose_water (gulkand is an alternative). 1 tbsp is soaked gond katira (jelly), not dry.

name: Variyali Sharbat (Gujarati Fennel Cooler)
steps: Powder 2 tbsp fennel seeds and lightly crush half a clove with a mortar and pestle.
Steep the powdered fennel and crushed clove in 1 cup (240 ml) water for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Strain the liquid and stir in 1.25 tbsp powdered mishri (rock sugar; sugar or honey also works) until dissolved.
Pour into a tall glass, add a few ice cubes and serve.
verified_note: Page lists 1/4 cup fennel, 2.5 tbsp mishri, 1 clove for 2 servings (halved). Water: method says 2 cups (ingredient list says 2.5 cups); used 2 cups halved. Mishri mapped to simple_syrup. No lemon or cardamom on the page.

name: Buransh Juice (Himalayan Rhododendron)
steps: Mix 1 part Buransh concentrate with 4 parts chilled water: about 50 ml concentrate with about 200 ml chilled water. Taste and sweeten lightly with sugar or honey if desired.
Add 1/2 tbsp lemon juice and stir well.
Add ice cubes and drop in a few mint leaves.
Optional: top up with a splash of soda water for a fizzy version.
Serve immediately.
