Mint 'a few sprigs' has no exact amount; 3 leaves is an estimate for garnish. Page also has a fresh-petal method (simmer 1 cup petals in water at 80C for 20 minutes) which was not used. Sugar/honey and soda optional, left out. Not included: Buransh (rhododendron) concentrate/squash, about 50 ml

name: Punjabi Sweet Malai Lassi
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup chilled plain yogurt in a bowl until smooth and creamy.
Add about 80 ml (1/3 cup) chilled water, 1 tbsp sugar and 1/4 tsp cardamom powder. Whisk vigorously until frothy and the sugar dissolves.
Pour into a tall glass and add a few ice cubes.
Garnish with slivered nuts and dried rose petals. Optionally top with a thick layer of malai.
garnish: slivered nuts and dried rose petals
verified_note: Divided by 3. Page has a cardamom discrepancy (1 tsp in list, 1/2 tsp in method); 1/4 tsp per serving used. Malai is optional with no amount, so cream left out. Our milk was dropped as page uses water.

name: Alphonso Mango Lassi
steps: If using fresh mangoes (Alphonso is best), chill them for a few hours, then peel and cube about 140 g (3/4 cup). If using canned Alphonso pulp, use about 1/2 cup and skip this step.
Add the mango, about 87 g (1/3 cup) cold plain yogurt, 90 ml (1/3 cup) cold milk (or water, or 2 ice cubes), 1/8 tsp cardamom powder and 3/4 to 1.5 tbsp sugar to a blender.
Blend until very smooth, thick but still pourable.
Taste and adjust: more sugar for sweetness, more milk or ice to thin, more mango for stronger flavor.
Pour into a glass. Refrigerate about 1 hour if you want it colder, and garnish with chopped pistachios or a pinch of saffron.
verified_note: Page serves 2, all amounts halved. Chopped mango/canned pulp mapped to mango_pulp in grams. Sugar 3/4 to 1.5 tbsp mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp (middle). Page gives yogurt in grams (175 g), halved to 87.

name: Gulkand Rose Lassi
steps: Add 3/4 cup (about 180 ml) chilled yogurt, 1/4 cup (60 ml) chilled milk, 1 tbsp gulkand, 0.75 tbsp rose syrup and 0.25 tsp cardamom powder to a blender.
Blend for about 2 minutes.
Pour the lassi into a glass.
Sprinkle with 0.5 tsp edible dried rose petals and 0.5 tbsp chopped pistachios and cashews, then drizzle with a little more rose syrup.
Serve right away, or refrigerate for 30 minutes first.
garnish: edible dried rose petals, chopped pistachios and cashews, extra rose syrup drizzle
verified_note: Source makes 2 and is divided by 2: yogurt 1.5 cups = 360 ml / 2 = 180 ml; milk 1/2 cup / 2 = 60 ml; gulkand 1/8 cup (2 tbsp) / 2 = 1 tbsp. Pistachios and cashews mapped to nuts. Extra rose syrup drizzle has no stated amount and is not included in ings.

name: Namkeen Pudina Lassi
steps: Put 120 ml yogurt, 1/4 cup washed and chopped mint leaves, 1/2 chopped green chilli and 1/4 teaspoon black salt (optional) in a blender jar.
Blend for 2-3 minutes until smooth.
Add a few ice cubes and blend again for a few seconds until frothy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.
verified_note: Original 1 cup curd, 1/2 cup mint, 1 green chilli, 1/2 tsp black salt for 2; halved. Green chilli mapped to chili. Ice blended in, no extra water.

name: Tadka Chaas (Tempered Buttermilk)
steps: Whisk 1/4 cup (60 ml) chilled plain yogurt in a bowl until smooth and creamy.

Add 1/4 tbsp chopped cilantro, 1/8 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/8 tsp black salt, 1/8 tsp regular salt, 1/8 tsp dry ginger powder, 1/8 tsp black pepper powder and 3/4 cup (180 ml) chilled water. Mix well.
Heat 3/4 tsp ghee in a small pan over medium heat.
When the ghee is hot, add 1/8 tsp cumin, 1/4 tsp chopped green chilies and 2 to 3 curry leaves. Let them crackle for 4 to 5 seconds.
Pour the tempering over the chaas and mix well.
Serve chilled over ice.
verified_note: Divided by 4. Black salt 1/8 tsp + regular salt 1/8 tsp combined as black_salt:0.25tsp. Dry ginger powder mapped to ginger. Curry leaves mapped to mustard_seed (tempering id). Cumin 1/8 roasted + 1/8 tempering = 0.25tsp. Ghee (3/4 tsp) has no id. Not included: ghee 0.75tsp

name: Sambharam / Neer Mor (South Indian Buttermilk)
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup (120 ml) yogurt with 3/4 cup (180 ml) water until thin.
Gently pound 1/4 tsp grated ginger, 1/4 tsp chopped green chilli (optional) and 1 to 2 curry leaves to release their juices.
Stir the pounded mixture into the buttermilk and add salt to taste.
Serve chilled; it keeps a day or two in the fridge.
verified_note: Curry leaves mapped to mustard_seed (curry leaf tempering) as leaves. Salt mapped to black_salt. Source makes 4 glasses; divided by 4.

name: Awadhi Mattha
steps: Put 120 ml curd, 1/4 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp powdered sugar, 1/4 tsp jeera (cumin) powder, a small piece of ginger (about 1/4 inch) and 3 mint leaves in a blender, with a few ice cubes.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass, serve chilled, and garnish with a mint sprig if you like.
verified_note: Source (2 cups curd, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp powdered sugar, 1 tsp jeera powder, 1 in ginger, 5 sprigs mint for 4) divided by 4; 1 cup taken as 240 ml. Salt mapped to black_salt. Source uses no water, only ice cubes, so total is small (~120 ml plus melted ice). Ginger amount approximated as grated tsp. Sprigs approximated as leaves.

name: Strawberry Cardamom Lassi
steps: Add 113 g (4 oz) hulled, roughly chopped fresh strawberries, 2 tbsp (30 ml) milk, 1/2 cup (125 g) plain whole milk yogurt, 1 tbsp (12.5 g) sugar, 1/8 tsp rosewater, 1/8 tsp ground cardamom and 1/2 cup (75 g) ice to a blender.
Blend until smooth and evenly combined.
Taste and adjust spices and sugar, then serve right away in a chilled glass.
verified_note: Page serves 2 to 4; I divided by 2 (page range for rosewater is 1/4 to 1/2 tsp, so 1/8 to 1/4 tsp used). Ice not listed as an ingredient. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Banarasi Thandai
steps: Make the paste (1/8 of the original batch): in a bowl put about 30 ml warm water with 4 g almonds, 2.5 g pistachios, 1/4 tsp white poppy seeds, 4 g melon seeds, 1/4 tbsp rose petals, 0.4 tsp fennel seeds and a pinch of whole black pepper. Mix, cover and let sit 1 to 2 hours (or 4 to 5 hours in the fridge; overnight is fine at room temperature).

Pour the whole mixture including the soaking water into a blender. Add about 1 tbsp (12 g) sugar, the seeds of half a green cardamom and 2 saffron strands. Grind to a very smooth, fine paste with no extra water (strain if not fine enough).
Put the paste (the original uses about 4 tbsp of paste per glass, adjust to taste) in a glass and add about 250 ml chilled milk.
Mix well, taste, and add more sugar if needed. Add a few ice cubes if you like.
Garnish with rose petals, chopped almonds or pistachios and serve immediately.
garnish: rose petals, chopped almonds or pistachios
verified_note: Source batch (8 cups milk, 1 cup soaking water, 3 tbsp almonds, 2 tbsp pistachios, 2 tbsp poppy seeds, 1/4 cup melon seeds, 2 tbsp rose petals, 1 tbsp fennel, 1/2 tsp pepper, 3-4 cardamoms, 15-18 saffron strands, 1/2 cup sugar) divided by 8; 1 cup = 250 ml. Almonds, pistachios, melon seeds and poppy seeds combined into nuts:10g. Soaking water is ground into the paste, so it is not extra volume beyond ~30 ml. Pepper amount about 0.06 tsp rounded to a pinch.

name: Kesar Badam Milk
steps: Soak a pinch of saffron (5 to 6 strands) in about 1.5 tsp hot milk or water for 15 minutes.
Blend about 8 soaked, peeled almonds into a coarse or smooth paste.
Heat 250 ml full-fat milk in a heavy-bottomed pan, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 5 minutes.
Stir in the almond paste continuously until well mixed, add the saffron water and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally so it does not stick.
Add 1.5 tsp sugar, 0.2 tsp cardamom powder and 0.25 tsp rose water (the page says 2-3 drops rose essence or 1 tsp rose water per litre), mix well and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove from heat and pour into a glass. Serve hot, or cool and chill for a few hours. Garnish with slivered almonds, pistachios and saffron strands.
garnish: slivered almonds, pistachios and saffron strands
verified_note: Page gives no serving count, only 1 litre milk; divided by 4 for a 250 ml serving. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup in tsp. Almonds mapped to nuts in pcs (30 almonds / 4).

name: Madurai Jigarthanda
steps: Rinse 1 tsp badam pisin (almond gum) in a bowl; crush it first if the pieces are large.
Add 1 cup water, cover and soak overnight or 8 to 9 hours until it swells and turns jelly-like. If it is too tight add a little more water.
Strain off the extra water and set the soaked badam pisin aside (rinse in the strainer if it has impurities).
Whisk 2 tbsp condensed milk into 1 cup (240 ml) chilled milk until mixed.
In a glass add 2 to 3 tbsp of the soaked badam pisin, then 2 to 3 tsp nannari syrup.
Pour in the condensed milk and milk mixture (about 1 cup).
Add 1 scoop vanilla ice cream and drizzle a little more nannari syrup over the top. Optionally add dry fruits, tutti frutti or glazed cherries.
Serve immediately.
garnish: dry fruits, tutti frutti or glazed cherries (optional)
verified_note: Page batch: 2 tsp badam pisin soaked in 2 cups water, 2 cups chilled milk, 4 tbsp condensed milk, 4 tsp nannari syrup, 2 scoops ice cream; divided by 2 (glass uses about 1 cup of the milk mixture). Badam pisin mapped to gond_katira (dry weight, soaked); ice cream scoop = 1 pcs. Rose syrup is the page's alternative to nannari.

name: Mohabbat Ka Sharbat (Old Delhi Watermelon Milk)
steps: Put 80 ml chilled whole milk, 2 teaspoons sugar and 1/2 tablespoon Rooh Afza in a glass or jug and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add about 40 ml fresh watermelon juice, about 3 tablespoons finely cubed watermelon (1/4-inch cubes) and 40 ml chilled water. Stir well.
Add a few ice cubes and 2 fresh rose petals as garnish.
Serve chilled.
verified_note: Original makes 6: divided by 6. watermelon:80 = about 40 ml juice plus about 40 ml (1/6 cup) cubes combined. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:2tsp.

name: Kesar Pista Falooda
steps: Soak 0.67 tsp sabja (basil) seeds in about 4 tbsp (60 ml) water for 20 to 30 minutes, then drain through a tea strainer.
Prepare 1 tbsp falooda sev (dry) as the package says: some types only need soaking in warm water, or boil it like noodles until soft. Drain and let it cool.
Coarsely crush about 1 tsp pistachios with a mortar and pestle.
In a small saucepan combine 85 ml (about 1/3 cup) milk and 1 to 1.33 tbsp sugar, then add the crushed pistachios and 8 to 10 crushed saffron strands (a pinch of cardamom powder is optional).
Heat on low, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Keep it warm but do not boil. Cool completely, or refrigerate if assembling later.
In a glass put half of the drained sabja seeds, then half of the falooda sev, then add 2 to 3 ice cubes.
Pour in the saffron-pistachio milk, then add the remaining sabja seeds and falooda sev.
Top with 1 to 2 scoops of vanilla ice cream (kesar or pista ice cream also works).
Garnish with about 1 tsp chopped pistachios, a few sliced cashews or almonds and a glazed cherry. Serve immediately.
garnish: chopped pistachios, sliced cashews or almonds, glazed cherry
verified_note: Page batch (1 cup milk, 3-4 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp pistachios + 1 tbsp garnish, 25-30 saffron strands, 2 tsp sabja, 3 tbsp falooda sev) divided by 3. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup; pistachios/cashews/almonds to nuts; saffron strands approximated as 1 pinch; sabja amount is dry. Page assembly steps use larger per-glass amounts of sabja/sev (1-2 tbsp each, soaked) than the batch list divided by 3. Glazed cherry and optional cardamom omitted from ings.

name: Banarasi Paan Shot
steps: Rinse 2 betel leaves well and drain.
Soak 1/2 tsp sabja (basil) seeds in enough water for 20 to 30 minutes, then drain through a fine strainer.
Puree the betel leaves in a small blender with about 1 tbsp water.
In a glass or jar, mix the puree with about 330 ml almond milk (or your preferred milk) until well combined.
Stir in 1.5 tbsp gulkand until evenly mixed.
Add the drained sabja seeds and 1 tsp rose syrup (optional), then 1 tbsp chopped dry fruits such as almonds or pistachios (optional).
Mix well and serve in a tall glass, or chill and serve later.
verified_note: Source (6-7 betel leaves, 4 cups almond milk, 1/2 tbsp sabja, 1 tbsp rose syrup, 4-5 tbsp gulkand, 2-3 tbsp dry fruits, 2-3 tbsp water for puree) divided by 3; 1 cup taken as 250 ml (333 ml, rounded to 330). Betel leaf mapped to herbal_leaf. Source says serve in tall glasses, not shot glasses.

name: Chikoo (Sapota) Milkshake
steps: Peel 1 1/2 medium chikoo, cut in half, remove the black seeds and roughly chop the flesh. Add it to a blender.
Taste a small piece of the fruit and add sugar according to its sweetness (about 1 to 1 1/2 tsp).
Add 3/4 cup (180 ml) chilled milk.
Blend until smooth, then pour into a serving glass.
verified_note: Source makes 2 (3 medium or 1 1/2 cups chikoo, 2-3 tsp sugar, 1 1/2 cups milk), halved. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page uses no ice (chilled milk keeps it cold) and names no glass.

name: Sitaphal (Custard Apple) Rabri Shake
steps: Halve 1 ripe custard apple (sitaphal) and scoop out the flesh. Put it in a blender with 1/4 cup of the cold milk and pulse a few times to separate the flesh from the seeds. Do not blend it smooth.
Pick the seeds out of the blender jar.
Add 1 tbsp sugar and the remaining 3/4 cup cold milk, then blend until frothy.
Pour into a glass and serve right away.
verified_note: Page is a plain custard apple milkshake, not a rabri version (no published sitaphal rabri shake found; the sitaphal rabdi page is a milk-reduction dessert). Custard apple has no id so it is unmapped. 1 cup milk = 240 ml. Not included: custard apple pulp (1 ripe custard apple)

name: Anjeer Badam Shake (Fig & Almond)
steps: Put about 2-3 dried figs in a bowl, add about 40 ml (1/6 cup) of the chilled milk, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until the figs puff up and soften.
Chop the soaked figs and 3-4 almonds and put them in a blender jar.
Add the leftover soaking milk and about 1 1/3 tsp sugar.
Blend until smooth, adding 2 ice cubes if you want it colder.
Add the rest of the chilled milk (about 160 ml) and blend until smooth. Strain if you dislike bits.
Pour into a glass, garnish with about 4 almond halves and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page serves 3, divided by 3: 8 figs = 2.7, 10 almonds = 3.3, 2.5 cups milk = 600 ml /3 = 200 ml, 4 tsp sugar = 1.3 tsp (page also suggests dates or 3 tsp honey as alternatives). Garnish almonds (12 halves /3 = 4) not in ings. Ice cubes optional, skipped.

name: Ganne Ka Ras (Spiced Sugarcane Juice)
steps: Peel the hard outer skin from 1 cup of sugarcane and chop it into small cubes.
Put the cubes and a small piece of ginger (about 1/4 inch) in a mixer jar, add a little water and grind. Work in batches if your jar is small.
Pour the mixture through a strainer, pressing the pulp with your hands or a spoon to catch the juice in a bowl. If the pulp still seems juicy, grind it again, then discard it.
Strain the collected juice once more to remove small sugarcane pieces.
Squeeze in a quarter of a lemon, add a tiny pinch of salt if using, and mix well.
Serve immediately in a glass, with a few ice cubes if you like.
verified_note: Source starts from 2 cups cubed sugarcane for 2 glasses and gives no juice volume; 150 ml juice per serving comes from the page's nutrition label (150 ml per serving). Page uses 1/8 to 1/4 cup water in total for grinding (not listed in ings). Ginger 1/2 inch piece / 2 is about 1.5 g (estimate). Salt is plain salt, mapped to black_salt. Lemon 1/2 / 2 = 0.25 lemon.

name: Elaneer Shake (Tender Coconut Milkshake)
steps: Put 2 tbsp (1/8 cup) sweetened condensed milk into a blender.
Add 1/2 cup tender coconut flesh.
Add sugar to taste.
Add 1 cup milk.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Transfer to a serving glass and serve cold.
verified_note: Halved from 2 servings. Page gives only coconut flesh (no coconut water), mapped to tender_coconut. Sugar is 'to taste' with no amount, so left out of ings.

name: Falsa Sharbat (Sherbet Berry Juice)
steps: Wash 125 g falsa (phalsa) berries and mash them with a spatula to separate the pulp from the seeds.
Blend the pulp with 1 tbsp sugar, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp black salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Strain the mixture into a bowl, pour the juice into a glass and add water to taste.
Add ice cubes and 0.5 tbsp chopped mint, then garnish with a lemon slice and mint leaves and serve.
verified_note: Falsa/phalsa mapped to berries (mixed berries). Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Page gives no water amount (only 'a little water' to blend and water to taste), so water is not listed in ings.

name: Jamun Shots (Black Plum Cooler)
steps: Remove the seeds from 3 to 4 jamun (Indian blackberry) and put the fruit in a grinder.
Add about 2 tsp jaggery powder, 1 tsp (4 ml) lemon juice and about 1 ice cube, and blend until smooth.
Mix a pinch of black salt (kala namak) and a pinch of red chilli powder on a plate.
Rub a lemon wedge around the rim of a shot glass and dip the rim in the spice mixture.
Pour the jamun mixture into the rimmed shot glass and serve cold.
garnish: black salt and red chilli rim
verified_note: Page: 12-15 jamun, 2-3 tbsp jaggery powder, juice of 1/2 lemon, 5-6 ice cubes, black salt and red chilli powder to taste, for 4 servings; divided by 4. Jamun counted as pcs (whole fruit) although the id is pulp. Black salt and chilli amounts are 'to taste' on the page, pinch is an assumption. Blended ice cubes are skipped from ings.

name: Mosambi (Sweet Lime) Masala Juice
steps: Stir black salt, chaat masala, and lemon juice into sweet lime juice.
Add ice cubes immediately.
Serve fresh to prevent oxidation bitterness.

name: Watermelon Rooh Afza Mint Cooler
steps: Put some crushed ice in a tall glass.
Add 1.5 tbsp Rooh Afza and 3/4 cup finely chopped watermelon.
Pour in 3/4 cup cold water, stir and serve.
verified_note: Page Rooh Afza variation is 2 tbsp Rooh Afza, 1 cup chopped watermelon, 1 cup cold water, 2 tbsp crushed ice (about 510 ml); scaled to 75% to stay under 450 ml. Page has no mint, lime or black salt.

sub: Iconic Hot & Iced Teas, Coffees & Warm Tonics
name: Cutting Masala Chai
steps: In a mortar and pestle, lightly pound together 1/3 inch ginger, 1 cardamom pod, 1 clove, a pinch of pepper (about 1/6 tsp) and a small piece (about 1/6 inch) of cinnamon so the spices release their flavor.
Warm 240 ml water in a saucepan over medium heat. Once hot, add the crushed spices and boil 3 minutes to infuse.
Add 1 tsp tea powder and boil 2 minutes.
Add 1 tsp sugar and boil until it dissolves.
Add 80 ml milk and bring to a boil. Stir and boil 2 minutes.
Strain the chai into a small glass and serve hot.
verified_note: Page makes 3: divided by 3. Cloves per serving is 1.33, rounded to 1. Cinnamon (1/2 inch for 3) given as a pinch. Ginger in inches shown as 0.33pcs (1 inch = 1pcs).

name: Kashmiri Kahwa
steps: Bring 1.5 cups (360 ml) water to a boil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat.
Put 1/8 tsp saffron threads in your cup and pour in about 1 tbsp of the boiling water; let it steep.
Coarsely smash 5 cardamom pods and half a cinnamon stick in a mortar and pestle. Add them to the saucepan with 1 tsp sugar and boil about 8 minutes, until it reduces to about 1 cup.
Turn off the heat, stir in 1.5 tbsp dried rose petals (optional) and cover. After 1 minute, add 1 tsp green tea, cover and steep 1.5 to 2 minutes.
Put 1.5 tbsp chopped or crushed blanched almonds in the cup, strain the tea into it, garnish with a few rose petals and serve with a small spoon for the almonds.
verified_note: Page makes 2 cups (3 cups water, 1/4 tsp saffron, 10 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 tsp sugar, 3 tbsp rose petals, 2 tsp green tea, 3 tbsp almonds), halved. Saffron 1/8 tsp = 1 pinch; 0.5 cinnamon stick as 0.5pcs. Serving temperature not stated explicitly; hot implied. No clove or honey in source.

sub: Iconic Hot & Iced Teas, Coffees & Warm Tonics
name: Kashmiri Noon Chai (Pink Salt Tea)
steps: Boil 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the water and brew 1/2 tsp green tea leaves in it until frothy.
Add a tiny pinch (about 1/12 tsp) of baking soda and whisk hard for about 10 seconds.
Add the other 1/4 cup (60 ml) water and the seeds of half a cardamom pod, crushed to powder. Brew until the tea turns bright red.
On medium heat add 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and whisk to make a slight froth. The tea should turn dark pink. Add more or less milk to get the shade you like.
Add 1/8 tsp salt and stir well.
Pour into a cup and serve hot.
verified_note: Baking soda has no id (about 1/12 tsp, kept in steps only). Salt mapped to black_salt. Page gives 1/3 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt for 4 servings. Not included: baking soda

name: South Indian Filter Kaapi
steps: Make the decoction: fit the top perforated vessel of the South Indian filter onto the lower vessel. Add 3 tsp ground filter coffee (medium strength) to the top vessel and spread it evenly. Place the pressing disc on the powder.

Boil 1 cup water and gently pour it into the top vessel until it is about 3/4 full. Cover with the lid and wait 10 to 12 minutes until the decoction drips into the lower vessel. This makes enough decoction for 2 to 3 tumblers; cover it and set aside.
Heat 3/4 cup whole milk until it boils.
Put 2 tsp sugar in a tumbler (or to taste). Strain 1/4 to 1/3 cup of the boiling milk into the tumbler (strain to keep out the skin, or skip straining for the cream).
Add 1/4 to 1/3 cup of the decoction to the tumbler, adjusting to taste.
Pour the coffee back and forth between the tumbler and the dabarah 2 to 3 times from a height to dissolve the sugar and make foam. Do not do it more often or the coffee cools.
Serve immediately in the tumbler with the dabarah underneath.
verified_note: Dark decoction mapped to espresso. Page gives 1/4 to 1/3 cup (60-80 ml) each for milk and decoction; 70 ml each used as the midpoint. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup:2tsp. Decoction recipe makes 2-3 servings.

name: Haldi Doodh (Golden Turmeric Milk)
steps: Pour 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk into a pot and bring it to a gentle boil. If using optional whole spices (1 crushed green cardamom, a 1/4-inch piece of cinnamon, 1 crushed clove, a pinch of dried ginger), add them and boil for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the milk cool until slightly hot.
Add 1/8 tsp ground black pepper and 3/4 tsp turmeric powder and mix well.
Transfer to a cup, strain if you used whole spices, and add 1 tsp honey (only once the milk is warm, not hot). Drink warm.
verified_note: Turmeric 3/4 to 1 tsp and pepper 1/8 to 1/4 tsp: lower ends used. Sweetener (1 tsp sugar/jaggery/honey) is optional, mapped to honey. Optional spices omitted from ings.

name: Jamun Mint Mojito
steps: For one glass, gently press together about 4 mint leaves, a small lime wedge (about 1/12 of a lime), 2 tsp sugar and 2.5 ml (1/2 tsp) lime juice with a muddler until fragrant and the lime releases its juice. Only bruise the mint lightly with a few gentle presses.
Add about 40 g (3 tbsp) thawed jamun pulp and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Put the mixture (about 4 tbsp) in a 6 oz (180 ml) glass and add ice cubes.
Top with about 60 ml (1/4 cup) sparkling water.
Garnish with mint leaves and serve immediately, since the fizz fades quickly.
verified_note: Page makes 24 drinks from 1 kg thawed jamun pulp, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup mint leaves, 2 big limes in wedges, 1/4 cup lime juice, 1.5 L sparkling water; divided by 24 (mint 4 leaves is an estimate of 1/24 cup). Optional charcoal-ghee smoking step left out because it is a large-batch step. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Guava Chili Spritzer
steps: Rub the rim of a tall glass with a lemon wedge, then dip it in a mix of 1/2 tsp red chilli powder and salt.
Fill the glass to the top with ice.
Pour in 1/2 cup (120 ml) pink guava nectar, then top with 1/2 cup (120 ml) sparkling water or soda and stir gently.
Garnish with 1 slit fresh green chilli and serve immediately.
verified_note: Chili entry is the 1/2 tsp red chilli powder and salt rim mix (the salt part is not split out; the page gives no ratio). The slit green chilli is listed in garnish. The lemon wedge for rimming is not listed in the page's ingredients. 1/2 cup = 120 ml.

name: Lahori Zeera Soda
steps: Dry-roast 2.4 tsp cumin seeds and 0.3 tsp black peppercorns over medium heat for a few minutes, stirring often, until lightly browned.
Take off the heat and let the spices cool for 5 minutes, then grind to a fine powder.
In a nonstick pan combine the powder with 1.6 tbsp sugar, 0.4 tsp black salt, 0.4 tsp chaat masala and 1.6 tbsp water. Mix well.
Cook over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes (the page's time for the full batch), stirring often, until it becomes a thick syrup.
Remove from heat and strain through a fine-mesh strainer. This gives about 2 tbsp jeera syrup (leftover syrup keeps in a bottle up to a month; stir before use).
To assemble, put 3 to 4 ice cubes in a glass, add 1 tbsp lime juice and 2 tbsp of the syrup.
Top with chilled club soda, stir and serve immediately.
verified_note: Page is titled Jeera Soda (same drink as Lahori Zeera soda; no page titled Lahori Zeera Soda with quantities was found). Syrup ingredients are the page's 10-serving batch divided by 10 (1/2 cup cumin seeds, 1 tbsp peppercorns, 1 cup sugar, 4 tsp black salt, 4 tsp chaat masala, 1 cup water); water is boiled down in the syrup so it is left out of ings. Page gives no soda amount ('chilled club soda, as needed'); 150 ml is an assumed fill. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup.

name: Anardana Lemonade
steps: Crush anardana seeds and steep in warm water for 15 minutes.
Strain liquid into ice-filled glass.
Add lemon juice, sugar, black salt, and top with chilled water.

name: Kamrakh (Starfruit) Mint Sharbat
steps: Add 1 starfruit (kamrakh), about 1 tbsp mint leaves, 0.5 tbsp lemon juice, 0.5 tsp salt, 0.5 tsp black salt, 0.5 tsp chaat masala, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 to 1.5 tbsp water to a blender and blend.
Pour the blended mixture into a 60 ml shot glass.
Fill a larger glass almost to the top with chilled soda and drop the shot glass into it. Serve.
verified_note: Page makes 2 shots; divided by 2. Starfruit has no id (unmapped). 1 tbsp mint leaves approximated as 5 leaves. Plain salt (0.5 tsp) omitted from ings; black salt kept. Page says 2-3 tbsp water for 2, so 1 to 1.5 tbsp. Soda amount 'as required', 150 ml assumed. Closest published starfruit-mint-soda drink found, not an exact 'sharbat'. Not included: starfruit (1 whole fruit)

name: Hing & Pudina Lemon Fizz
steps: Muddle mint with lemon juice, hing, cumin, and salt.
Add ice cubes to highball glass.
Pour cold soda over ice and stir once.

name: Phalsa Mint Sparkler
steps: Add falsa concentrate and lime juice to a glass over ice.
Slap mint leaves and drop inside.
Top with sparkling water and stir.

name: Spicy Tamarind Ginger Cooler
steps: Tamarind tea: bring 1/2 cup water to a boil, add about 1.75 oz (50 g) tamarind pulp, reduce to medium-low, cover and simmer 15 minutes, stirring halfway through to break it up.
Press the tamarind through a fine sieve with the back of a spoon and discard the solids. You should have about 1/3 cup (80 ml) puree.
Stir in a small pinch of salt and 2/3 cup (150 ml) water to make the tamarind tea.

Ginger syrup: in a small saucepan combine 2 tbsp thinly sliced unpeeled ginger, 2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp water. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low, cover and simmer about 25 minutes until the ginger is soft and the syrup is very fragrant. Discard the ginger and let the syrup cool.
To serve, pour the tamarind tea and 3 tbsp (45 ml) ginger syrup into a tall glass filled with ice cubes.
Top with 1/4 to 1/2 cup club soda or sparkling water.
verified_note: Original makes 8 to 10 glasses (2.5 to 3 cups tamarind puree + 5 cups water, 1 cup tea per glass); I divided by 8. Tamarind mapped as pulp amount in ml. Soda is the midpoint of the 1/4 to 1/2 cup range (page also mentions an optional turbinado sugar rim, no amount given). Scaling is my estimate.

name: Karonda (Natal Plum) Sharbat
steps: Boil karondas with sugar and water until soft; crush and strain.
Chill the vibrant pink-red liquid.
Serve over ice with black salt and cumin.

name: Kokum Ginger Sparkling Mule
steps: Mix kokum agal, ginger syrup, and honey in a glass base.
Fill with ice cubes.
Top with chilled soda water and stir gently.

name: Raw Mango Cardamom Punch
steps: Peel and dice 1/2 raw unripe mango and pressure cook it with a little water for 2 to 3 whistles. Let it cool, then blend into a smooth puree.
Blend in 2 tbsp jaggery or sugar, a small pinch of salt (about 1/8 tsp), 1/4 tsp black salt or chaat masala and 1/8 tsp black pepper.
Add 1/8 tsp cardamom powder (the page says cardamom or cumin, not both).
Stir in about 300 ml cold water and 1 chopped mint leaf. Add 1/2 to 1 tsp lemon juice if you want it more tart. Strain if you do not want pulp.
Chill and serve over ice.
verified_note: Classic aam panna used as the real published raw-mango cardamom drink. Halved from 2 servings; water reduced from 1.5-2 cups to 300 ml to stay under 450 ml. Plain salt folded into black_salt (0.125 + 0.25 tsp).

name: Masala Orange Spritz
steps: Stir chaat masala and black salt into fresh orange juice.
Add ice to glass.
Top with club soda and stir softly.

name: Sweet & Spicy Pineapple Panna
steps: Heat a non-stick or cast-iron pan on medium-high. Add 1/2 cup pineapple cubes dry and grill 6 to 8 minutes until lightly charred on both sides. Let cool to room temperature.

Add the cooled pineapple, 2 tbsp packed mint leaves, a tiny piece of ginger (about 1/8 inch), 3/4 tbsp powdered jaggery, 1/8 tsp black salt, 3/4 tsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/8 tsp crushed black peppercorns and 1/4 cup (60 ml) water to a blender.
Blend on high for 60 to 90 seconds until smooth. Optionally strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing with a spoon.
Stir in the remaining 1/2 cup (120 ml) cold water, taste and adjust, then refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Fill a tall glass with ice, pour the panna over, and garnish with a mint sprig and a thin pineapple wedge. Serve immediately.
garnish: mint sprig and thin pineapple wedge
verified_note: Divided by 4. 1/2 cup mint = 2 tbsp = 0.125 cup. Ginger 1/8 inch converted approx to 0.25 tsp chopped. Total water 3/4 cup = 180 ml. Pineapple is grilled, not juiced.

name: Nimbu Black Pepper Tonic
steps: In a glass, whisk 30 ml (2 tbsp) fresh lime juice with 2 tbsp sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Add 250 ml chilled seltzer, 1/8 tsp coarsely ground black pepper and 1/8 tsp kosher salt, and stir in.
Pour over ice.
verified_note: Closest published recipe is Saveur's Nimbu Pani with black pepper, not a drink called 'Tonic'. Seltzer = soda_water; sugar = simple_syrup (2 tbsp dry sugar); kosher salt = black_salt (salt id). Page makes 2-4 servings, divided by 4.

name: Spicy Anardana Mint Cooler Crushed
steps: In a tall glass, combine 1/4 cup pomegranate arils, 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.
Mash with a masher or spoon until the sugar dissolves and the arils release their juice.
Add 3 ice cubes to the glass.
Top with 1 1/2 cups sparkling water (or lemon-lime soda), stir gently and serve.
verified_note: Page uses fresh pomegranate arils, not dried anardana; arils mapped to pomegranate_juice by volume. Page says 1 tsp salt (regular); mapped to black_salt. Sugar mapped to simple_syrup. Total volume is close to the 450 ml limit.

name: Cucumber Mint Masala Fizz
steps: Muddle cucumber slices and mint in glass.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and ice cubes.
Top with club soda and stir gently.

name: Wood Apple Mint Fizz
steps: Stir bel pulp with simple syrup, cumin, and crushed mint.
Fill glass with ice cubes.
Top with cold club soda and mix gently.

name: Chandan (Sandalwood) Sharbat
steps: Make the syrup first (this is a batch that keeps up to 6 months in the fridge): heat 1/2 cup water in a small pan, and when it boils add 1 g saffron strands. Remove from heat and rest for 30 minutes.

In a large pan combine 1 liter water, 5 cups sugar and 3 tbsp fresh lime juice. Heat on medium-high, stirring often, until it boils. Lower the heat and cook 6-8 minutes, then strain through a fine-mesh strainer.
Stir in the saffron water, 2 tbsp edible-grade sandalwood (chandan) powder and 1 tsp citric acid until well mixed. Pour into a clean glass bottle and refrigerate.
For one serving: shake the bottle well, add 1 tbsp of the syrup to a glass and top with about 200 ml chilled water.
Add a few ice cubes and serve chilled.
verified_note: Page is a syrup recipe; per-glass instruction is 1 tbsp syrup topped with chilled water. Homemade kesar-chandan syrup mapped to simple_syrup. Amount of chilled water per glass is not stated; 200 ml assumed to fill a glass. Syrup steps are given as the page's batch amounts because they cannot be reduced to one glass. Not included: edible sandalwood powder (2 tbsp per batch), saffron (1 g per batch), citric acid (1 tsp per batch)

name: Mogra (Jasmine) Nectar Sharbat
steps: Concentrate (made ahead in a batch, keeps up to a month in the fridge): in a saucepan on medium heat combine 1 1/2 cups sugar and 3/4 cup water, bring to a rolling boil, lower the heat and stir in 1 teaspoon milk.
Skim off the impurities that float to the top with a tea strainer and discard them.
Add 1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder, a few saffron strands and 3/4 cup fresh jasmine buds.
Bring to a rolling boil again, switch off the heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Cover the pan and leave it for about 24 hours so the jasmine flavour infuses the syrup.
Strain out and discard the jasmine buds, then pour the syrup into a bottle and refrigerate.
To serve: put 1 tablespoon of the concentrate in a glass, add a few ice cubes and top with 200 ml water.
verified_note: The jasmine concentrate (sugar, cardamom, saffron, jasmine buds) is mapped to simple_syrup:1tbsp; no jasmine or batch ingredients are in the ingredient list. Not included: jasmine bud concentrate (batch)

name: Brahmi Cooling Tonic
steps: Blend 1/3 cup brahmi leaves with 1/3 tsp roasted cumin powder, a small pinch of black salt and a small pinch of freshly ground black pepper into a fine paste.
Add 2/3 tsp honey and 160 ml (2/3 cup) water, then mix well.
Serve chilled.

name: Parijat (Night Jasmine) Infusion

Serve over ice cubes.

name: Curry Leaf & Lemon Tonic
steps: Wash 5 to 7 fresh curry leaves and pat them dry with a kitchen towel, then chop them.
In a shaker bottle, add the chopped curry leaves and 2 to 3 fresh lime wedges.
Add 4 tsp lime juice and 3 tbsp simple sugar syrup (or adjust to taste).
Add plenty of ice cubes and shake vigorously.

name: Tulsi Ginger Honey Tonic
steps: Muddle tulsi leaves with ginger juice and honey.
Pour cold or warm water and stir until honey dissolves.
Strain and serve with a tulsi leaf float.

name: Hibiscus (Gudhal) Ruby Sharbat
steps: Put about 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp of dried hibiscus petals and 240 ml (1 cup) water in a saucepan.
Boil until the petals turn white and the water turns ruby red.
While it heats, soak 1 tsp basil (sabja) seeds in a little cold water in a small bowl until they bloom.
Turn off the heat and let the hibiscus liquid cool completely.
Strain out the petals, then stir in about 1.3 tbsp (20 ml) rose syrup.
Stir in the bloomed basil seeds.
Pour into a glass, top with ice and fresh mint.

name: Vetiver Rose Herbal Cooler
steps: Layer khus syrup and rose syrup in glass with ice.

name: Saunf Mishri Wellness Water
steps: Grind 2 tbsp saunf (fennel seeds), 2 tbsp mishri (rock sugar) and 5 black peppercorns into a fine powder.
In a glass, mix the powder with 1 cup cold water.
Add 1 tsp black salt and stir well.
Add 4 ice cubes and garnish with 4 sprigs of mint leaves. Serve chilled.

name: Lemongrass Ginger Iced Tonic

In a saucepan over high heat bring 1 1/3 cups (320 ml) water, the lemongrass, ginger and about 1 tbsp sugar to a boil.

Remove the tea, then let the mixture sit for about 30 minutes.
Pour through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher or jar.
Refrigerate until cool, about a couple of hours.
Pour over ice and top with a mint sprig.

name: Badian (Star Anise) Herbal Fizz

name: Bael Leaves Digestive Tea

name: Arjun Bark Cardiac Tonic
steps: Boil about 100 ml (half a glass) water for 1 minute on a low flame.

steps: Muddle tender neem leaves into fine paste with lemon juice.

name: Kanji (Fermented Black Carrot Drink)

name: Beetroot Masala Chaas

Sprinkle a small pinch of whole cumin (about 1/12 tsp) over the charcoal and pour a few drops of ghee (about 1/12 tsp) on top.
Cover with aluminium foil and let it rest for 2-3 minutes so the smoky aroma infuses into the chaas.
Serve with a few ice cubes and garnish with mint leaves.

steps: Mash roasted garlic cloves into a smooth paste.

steps: Chop 1 large yellow peach roughly and discard the stone.
Blend the peach flesh with the seeds of 5 crushed cardamom pods (or ground cardamom), 1 tsp honey and a pinch (1/8 tsp) of salt until smooth.
Add 1/2 cup (125 ml) Greek yoghurt and 1/2 cup (125 ml) cold milk and blend again until frothy.

name: Pineapple Mint Lassi Blended
steps: Grind 1/4 tsp cumin seeds to a fine powder with a mortar and pestle or in a blender (a pinch of coarse salt helps in a mortar).

Put ice cubes in a glass and pour the lassi over them.

name: Guava Red Chili Lassi Blended
steps: Blend guava pulp, yogurt, sugar, and cumin until smooth.

name: Kesar Badam Lassi Rich
steps: Warm 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the milk in the microwave for about 45 seconds and divide it between two small bowls.

Sieve the mixture into a glass and serve right away.

name: Blueberry Cardamom Lassi Blended
steps: Add 50 g blueberries to the blender jar and blend alone for 10-15 seconds to break them down.

name: Avocado Honey Lassi

name: Banana Elaichi Lassi
steps: Add 1/2 cup (125 ml) yogurt, 1 chopped banana, about 1 3/4 tbsp sugar, a small pinch (1/16 tsp) cardamom powder and about 80 ml chilled water to a blender.

name: Rose Sabja Lassi Seed

steps: Put 3/4 cup muskmelon (cantaloupe) chunks, 1/2 cup (120 ml) plain yogurt and about 2/3 tablespoon honey or sugar in a blender.

name: Saffron Honey Lassi
steps: In a skillet over low heat, crumble 1/8 tsp saffron threads into 30 ml (2 tbsp) water and let stand 5 minutes.

name: Tender Coconut Lassi Blended Curd
steps: Add 1/4 cup (about 60 g) curd, 1/4 cup grated fresh coconut, 2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp chopped mint (pudina) and 3/4 cup (about 155 ml) coconut water to a blender.

name: Spiced Hing Mattha
steps: Add about 1/3 cup (80 ml) plain yogurt to a bowl and pour in 2/3 cup (160 ml) chilled water. Blend or whisk until smooth and frothy.
Add 1/6 tsp roasted cumin powder, a tiny pinch (about 1/12 tsp) of minced ginger, about 1/12 tsp black salt, 2 tsp chopped mint or coriander leaves and a pinch of asafoetida (hing, optional).
Blend again for a few seconds until combined.
Pour into a glass, garnish with a little extra cumin and chopped herbs, and serve immediately while chilled.

name: Pune Mango Mastani Layered Shake &

name: Guava Chaat Cooler Pressed

Blend into a smooth puree, straining if needed to remove any unground seeds. Add water as needed to reach the thickness you like.
Soak 1 tsp sabja (sweet basil) seeds in 2 tbsp (30 ml) water for about 5 minutes until they swell, then stir them into the puree.
Serve cold.

Add 1 oz (30 ml) water and a splash (about 4 ml) of lime juice and blend until completely smooth.
Strain the juice into a glass and stir in a small sprinkle (about 1/16 tsp) of kala namak (black salt).
Garnish with mint and serve chilled.

name: Papaya Lime Mint Cooler Blended
steps: Blend 1/2 cup diced ripe papaya, about 1/8 cup fresh mint leaves and 2 tbsp cold water until smooth.
Strain the blend through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a glass or jug.
Add 60 ml (1/4 cup) lemon juice, 2 tbsp honey (or agave) and the remaining water (about 210 ml), and stir.
Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Refrigerate for at least 1 to 2 hours.
Add ice, stir and pour into a glass.

name: Mulberry (Shahtoot) Sharbat
steps: Put 80 g (about 3 oz) mulberries, 1 1/3 tablespoons jaggery powder and about 1/6 teaspoon rock salt in a small pan and add 80 ml water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Let the mixture cool to room temperature, then blend it.
Strain the smooth mixture into a jar and refrigerate for a few hours.
To serve, mix the sharbat with water and ice in a glass, adjusting to taste.

name: Lychee Rose Sparkler

Add 3 oz (90 ml) lychee juice from the tin, 3/4 oz (22 ml) rose syrup and 1/2 oz (15 ml) lime juice, with 3 to 4 ice cubes. Put the lid on and shake for 10 to 15 seconds.
Fill a glass with ice (add edible rose buds if you like) and strain the mixture in.
Top with 1/2 cup (120 ml) ginger kombucha or sparkling or still coconut water and stir gently.
Garnish with lychees, edible rose buds and/or a lime slice if desired.

name: Plum Mint Punch
steps: Remove the pits from 125 g plums, leaving the skins on.

Add 1 tbsp vanilla sugar, 250 ml fresh water and 1 to 2 mint leaves, and blend with a hand mixer until very liquid.
Add more water if you want a thinner juice, then pour into a tall glass.

name: Pomegranate Mint Elixir Pressed

Add 3 ice cubes, top with 1.5 cups sparkling water (or lemon-lime soda) and stir gently before serving.

name: Sulaimani Tea (Kerala Spiced Black Tea) Boiled
steps: Lightly crush 1 green cardamom, 1 clove, a 1/4 inch piece of cinnamon and a 1/2 inch piece of peeled ginger (optional) in a mortar and pestle.
Put 1 cup water and the crushed spices in a saucepan, bring to a boil on medium heat, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.

Add 1/2 tsp black tea. If using loose leaves, turn off the heat, cover and steep 2 to 3 minutes. If using tea powder or half a tea bag, simmer 2 to 3 minutes until the colour deepens, without over-boiling.
Stir in 4 tsp raw or white sugar until dissolved, then turn off the heat.
Stir in 1/2 tsp lemon juice (add a little more for more tang) and 4 to 5 mint leaves if using, cover and rest for about a minute.
Strain into a cup or glass and serve hot.

name: Chukku Kappi (Dry Ginger Coffee)

Add 0.75 tbsp jaggery and stir until it dissolves.
Add 0.75 tsp dry ginger powder, 0.25 tsp cumin seeds, 0.75 tsp instant coffee powder and 0.25 tsp black pepper. Boil for about 4 minutes.
Add 5 tulsi (holy basil) leaves and boil for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1 cardamom pod (or a pinch of cardamom powder) and a tiny pinch of salt, then turn off the heat.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.

name: Adrak Elaichi Chai Simmered
steps: Heat about 120 ml water in a saucepan over medium heat.
When the water forms little bubbles, add 1/2 tsp loose Indian tea leaves (or about 3/4 of a tea bag) and 3/4 tbsp sugar and stir well.
Let it boil about 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 150 ml milk. Once it starts to boil and the tea rises, lower the heat and simmer about 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 tbsp grated ginger and 1/4 tsp cardamom powder and boil about 5 minutes.
Strain into a cup and serve hot.

name: Gur Wali Chai (Jaggery Tea) Simmered

Add 1 tsp loose black tea leaves (a strong variety like CTC) and boil for 2 minutes, until the water darkens.
Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk and bring to a rolling boil, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and stir in 1 to 1.5 tbsp grated jaggery until it fully dissolves.
Simmer 2 to 3 more minutes, until the chai is a deep caramel brown.
Strain into a small glass and serve hot and strong.

Pour 160 ml (2/3 cup) water into a saucepan on medium heat. Add the crushed spices, 2 dried rose petals and 2 tsp sugar.
Bring to a gentle boil on medium heat, then turn off the heat and set the pan aside.
Add 1/3 tsp green tea leaves, cover and steep for 3 minutes.
Strain into a small cup. Add 3 to 4 saffron strands and the sliced almonds and stir. Serve hot.
